seeds.ex: A Microsoft 365 tenant holds Entra ID, the license pool, Teams policies, and the verified domains. Direct Routing will only pair an SBC FQDN that belongs to one of those verified domains. The default onmicrosoft.com domain is not eligible. Before you discuss codecs, say which tenant you are in and whether the users are homed online. Direct Routing is not supported in Islands mode.
seeds.eg: Name the tenant, the verified domain, and that onmicrosoft.com cannot be the SBC name.

seeds.ti: Entra ID accounts voice will use
seeds.ex: Humans, rooms, and resource accounts are Entra objects. Resource accounts are disabled for sign-in on purpose. They represent an auto attendant or a call queue. They are not a shared mailbox someone should open in Outlook as their daily driver. Create the object, license it, then grant voice policy. Creating a resource account takes a Teams administrator role and the User Administrator role.
seeds.eg: Resource accounts do not sign in. Humans and rooms do.

seeds.ex: Teams Administrator, Teams Telephony Administrator, and Teams Communications Administrator cover different slices of calling and meetings. Support Engineer and Support Specialist are troubleshooting roles, useful for Call Analytics, and the wrong tool for building a dial plan. Use the smallest role that can do the change. Keep named accounts. Conditional Access belongs on those admin accounts.
seeds.eg: I will use a telephony or Teams admin role, not a shared global admin.

seeds.ex: Numbers, voice routing, attendants, and queues are Teams admin center work, with PowerShell beside them. Licenses, including the Teams Phone Resource Account license, are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Emergency addresses and network topology sit with the voice configuration, not with a random SharePoint site. When the portal and the shell disagree, read the user with Get-CsOnlineUser.
seeds.eg: Licenses in one center, voice objects in the other, effective policy from the shell.

seeds.ex: Cloud Voicemail deposits the message in the user’s Exchange mailbox. No mailbox, no deposit. Overflow from a queue to voicemail fails the same way if the account that should receive the message has nowhere to put it. Debug voicemail only after the call has actually reached the voicemail path. If the ladder dies at the carrier, the mailbox is innocent.
seeds.eg: Cloud Voicemail needs a mailbox. The SBC cannot store the message for you.

seeds.ex: Direct Routing expects the user to be homed in Microsoft 365. Islands mode is explicitly unsupported for Direct Routing. Those are registrar and coexistence facts, not SBC opinions. Read the user before you assign a voice routing policy. If the pilot group is a mix of online users and leftover coexistence modes, you will debug one trunk twice and learn nothing. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Direct Routing users are homed online, and they are not in Islands mode.

seeds.ex: A person who places or receives PSTN calls needs Teams and Teams Phone, unless a bundle already includes that capability. Confirm the bundle on the licensing page, because names move. A Calling Plan, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing is the connectivity choice on top.
seeds.eg: Teams Phone is not a carrier. Name the connectivity option separately.

seeds.ex: Calling Plans make Microsoft the carrier. You pick a flavor that matches how the user dials, and you can only buy it where Microsoft sells it. Pay-as-you-go is also the funding pattern, with communications credits, for some voice-app outbound calls. A user in a country without Calling Plans needs Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing. Assigning a SKU that cannot be used is not a routing problem.
seeds.eg: Calling Plans are Microsoft as the carrier, sold only in some countries, in three usual flavors.

seeds.ex: Teams Premium adds meeting and related features. It does not replace Teams Phone, a Calling Plan, Audio Conferencing, or a resource-account license. If a proposal removes Calling Plans because Premium was purchased, the proposal is wrong. Say that out loud in the interview. Then go back to the connectivity option the users actually need. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Teams Premium does not include a phone system or a carrier.

seeds.ex: Each auto attendant or call queue that answers needs a resource account with a Microsoft Teams Phone Resource Account license, even when you do not assign a phone number. Tenants with Teams Phone get a zero-cost allotment, and you still have to acquire those licenses. Do not assign Teams Phone Standard to a resource account.
seeds.eg: Resource accounts get the Teams Phone Resource Account license, not Teams Phone Standard.

seeds.ti: Rooms, common area, and shared calling
seeds.ex: A common-area phone on Direct Routing does not need a Calling Plan. Teams Rooms use the current room SKU, not a borrowed user license. Shared Calling lets people place outbound calls through a resource account’s number, and it has its own funding rules. Read the current page for the pattern you are about to promise. Room names change.
seeds.eg: A Direct Routing common-area phone does not need a Calling Plan. A room has its own SKU.

seeds.ti: A license set you can defend
seeds.ex: Walk the picker in this order: does the person need PSTN, who is the carrier, do meetings need a dial-in number, is there a room, is there a voice app, does that app dial out. Audio Conferencing is the meeting dial-in. It is not implied by Teams Phone. End with the sentence that Teams Premium changed none of those answers.
seeds.eg: I separate Teams Phone, the carrier, Audio Conferencing, the resource account, and Premium.

seeds.ex: Install the MicrosoftTeams module and connect it to the tenant you named in the foundations track. Confirm you are not in production. Cmdlet parameters move between module versions, so Get-Help in the version you are about to run beats a blog post. Compliance recording policies are created and granted in this module. If you only learn the portal, you cannot finish a recorder design. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I connect the MicrosoftTeams module to a named tenant and read help before I change anything.

seeds.ex: A dial plan holds normalization rules. A voice route holds a pattern and gateways. A PSTN usage is a name that ties routes to a policy. A voice routing policy is the ordered list of usages you grant to a user. A PSTN gateway is the paired SBC. Application instances show up twice in real designs: resource accounts for voice apps, and bots for compliance recording.
seeds.eg: Usage, route, policy, gateway. The policy is what the user has. The route is what the pattern does.

seeds.ex: New-CsOnlineVoiceRoute creates a route. Set-CsOnlinePstnUsage maintains the usage list. Grant-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy assigns a policy to a user. Grant-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy assigns a recorder policy. None of those verbs is a synonym. Read with Get- before you Set- or Grant-. Then read again. The second read is the evidence pack, not a personality trait. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Grant assigns to a user. Set changes an object. I read both times.

seeds.ti: Reading a user before you change one
seeds.ex: Get-CsOnlineUser shows voice policy, dial plan, and number fields. Look at the effective values. A group grant can beat the direct assignment you remember from last quarter. Test the call as that user, from the client they actually use. A browser join and a certified phone do not take the same media path, and QoS will not treat them the same either. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I read the effective policy with Get-CsOnlineUser before I edit anything.

seeds.ti: When the portal and the shell disagree
seeds.ex: If the Teams admin center shows a policy and the shell shows another, believe the shell long enough to place a test call, then refresh both. Replication delay is real. An hour of firmware changes during that delay is not. Write down the time, the cmdlet, and the values. That note is the evidence pack. It is also how you avoid changing three systems because one screen was stale. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I will trust a fresh Get- over a stale toast, then place one test call.

seeds.ex: Pair a lab SBC to a lab domain. Use obviously fake names. Contoso and 555 numbers exist so practice does not point at a real directory. Do not find-and-replace a lab script onto production without reading every name. Production changes get one hypothesis, a rollback, and a window. The lab is where you learn that a private CA will not satisfy Direct Routing. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I will not discover certificate behavior on the company trunk.

seeds.ex: Microsoft’s QoS and network articles tell you to keep the path short: on the order of three to five hops from the client to your edge, and a short path from the ISP to Microsoft. Proxies in the media path are a known way to damage calls. ExpressRoute is not required. Draw the path a branch actually uses. If that branch backhauls across a continent to egress, you already know why RTT is high.
seeds.eg: Local egress, no media proxy, ExpressRoute not required.

seeds.ex: The QoS article’s initial ranges are audio UDP or TCP 50000–50019 at DSCP 46 EF, video 50020–50039 at 34 AF41, sharing 50040–50059 at 18 AF21, and calling and meeting signaling 50070–50089 at 40 CS5. Signaling ports are not configurable. Browser joins do not use those fixed ranges. Mac and mobile hard-code audio as EF.
seeds.eg: Audio is 46 on ports 50000 to 50019. I can place the other three without a card.

seeds.ex: Microsoft recommends that you avoid real-time media on a VPN. QoS inside the tunnel only prioritizes traffic inside a path that is already longer. Split tunnel is the usual way to let media go direct while other traffic stays on the VPN. A VPN pool labeled as headquarters will make CQD accuse the wrong building and can make dynamic emergency calling report the wrong place.
seeds.eg: I keep real-time media off the full-tunnel VPN, and I do not label the VPN pool as HQ.

seeds.ex: G.711 at 20 milliseconds is 160 bytes of payload. Add 40 bytes of IP, UDP, and RTP and the call is 80 kbit/s per direction at layer 3. Add an 18-byte Ethernet header and it is 87.2 kbit/s. G.729 at the same interval is 20 bytes of payload, 24 kbit/s at layer 3. Silence suppression and a different packet interval change the average.
seeds.eg: G.711 at 20 ms is 80 kbit/s at layer 3 and 87.2 with a typical Ethernet header.

seeds.ex: Capture at the network egress, not only on the PC. You want the DSCP value on the wire after the VPN, the switch, and the router. Port mirroring is the usual way. If audio ports 50000–50019 leave the building marked 0, the client policy missed or a device rewrote the mark. Fix that before you argue about codecs. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I capture at the egress and show DSCP 46 still on the audio ports.

seeds.ex: Teams is designed to work over the internet with local egress. If your organization also has ExpressRoute, follow the current network documentation for which traffic belongs there. Do not assume media is automatically better on the private path. QoS still has to be consistent on whatever path you chose. A private path with no marks and extra distance is a slower best-effort network. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Teams does not require ExpressRoute. Local internet egress is the normal plan.

seeds.ti: Four ways to reach the PSTN
seeds.ex: The four options on the connectivity page are Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. The others use a partner or your SBC. One tenant may use all four for different people. Operator Connect for India is its own plan because the regulatory problem is different. Do not hide an India office inside a UK SBC and call it Operator Connect.
seeds.eg: Four options. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. Mixing them in one tenant is allowed.

seeds.ex: You assign the plan, you receive numbers from Microsoft, and emergency calling in supported countries is part of that service. You still configure emergency locations. You do not pair an SBC for those users. If a Calling Plan user also matches a Direct Routing voice route, you may send their calls onto your SBC by accident. The policy has to match the license. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Calling Plan users should not inherit a Direct Routing route by accident.

seeds.ex: The operator is enabled in the tenant and assigns numbers. You need Teams Phone. You do not need a Microsoft Calling Plan, and you do not run the SBC. India has a separate operator plan. Ask the operator which numbers are service numbers for attendants and which are user numbers. A user number that walks out the door with an employee is a publishing problem. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Operator Connect is Teams Phone plus a certified carrier. I do not also build an SBC for those same numbers.

seeds.ex: Teams Phone Mobile uses a certified mobile operator. The user’s SIM number is assigned as their Teams number. They need Teams Phone. They do not need a separate Calling Plan for that path. Do not put the main queue on someone’s SIM. When that person leaves, the number leaves. CRM matching also fails if the same human presents two caller IDs. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Teams Phone Mobile makes the SIM number the Teams number. I would not put a queue on it.

seeds.ex: You pair an SBC FQDN on a verified domain, present a public certificate, signal TLS to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com and its sip2 and sip3 partners on port 5061, and allow media UDP 3478–3481 and 49152–53247. Firewall rules must allow the published IP ranges, not only today’s DNS answer. GCC High and DoD use different proxy names. Users need Teams and Teams Phone, homed online, not in Islands mode.
seeds.eg: 5061 to the three commercial proxies, media on those UDP ranges, certificate name matches the FQDN, user has a route.

seeds.ex: Write a table: population, connectivity, policy, who operates the trunk. A contact center on Direct Routing and a headquarters on Operator Connect is a normal tenant, not a compromise. The failure mode is a single voice routing policy granted to everyone. Mobile users then hairpin through an SBC they should never touch, or Calling Plan emergency calls leave the country. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I mix options on purpose, with a policy per population.

seeds.ex: The person dials 020 7555 4010 or 425 555 0100. The first matching normalization rule rewrites it. Later rules do not run. The voice route then sees the result, usually E.164. Put emergency short codes above any catch-all. A rule that turns every three-digit string into an extension will eat 999. Test the raw digits and the normalized form. The route is not wrong just because you typed the raw digits into it.
seeds.eg: First matching normalization rule wins. I test the route with the normalized number.

seeds.ex: Tenant dial plans hold the rules. Grant the plan to the users it describes. A user with a specific plan will not pick up your edit to the global plan. Keep rules anchored. A pattern without an end anchor will match a prefix of a longer number and translate the wrong thing. The lab on this campus is a teaching matcher with the same first-match idea, not the Microsoft service. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Specific rules first, grant the plan to the user, test as that user.

seeds.ex: PSTN usages are names. Voice routes attach to them. The user’s voice routing policy lists the usages in order. Teams walks that order. This campus’s matcher does the same and says so on the lab. Give a branch a policy whose usages stop at national. Give headquarters a policy that continues to international. Do not share one policy and hope the route patterns save you. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: The usage is the permission. The policy is the ordered list of permissions on the user.

seeds.ex: Anchor the pattern to the normalized number. List gateways with priorities. In this campus, priority 1 is tried first. Confirm the current article before you depend on a production tie-break. A second gateway that has never carried a call is a drawing. Unassigned numbers you own should be treated on purpose, usually toward an attendant. A ported block with fifty silent numbers looks like an outage.
seeds.eg: The voice route is a regex and a gateway list. I rehearse failover.

seeds.ex: A London user dials a UK national number. Their dial plan emits +44. Their policy lists emergency, then UK national, then international. The UK route matches +44 and prefers sbc-lon, with sbc-man as priority 2. A Manchester-only policy has no international usage, so a US number fails closed.
seeds.eg: I can walk one number through normalize, usage, route, and gateway.

seeds.ti: Islands mode and other hard stops
seeds.ex: Direct Routing is not supported in Islands mode. An SBC FQDN on onmicrosoft.com is not supported. A private CA is not a production certificate. AMR-WB is not a bypass codec. Media cannot be re-targeted mid-call. Memorize the hard stops. They save you from debugging a dial plan that was never going to run. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I list the hard stops before I tune a regex.

seeds.ex: Create the resource account, assign the Teams Phone Resource Account license, and attach it to the attendant or queue. A phone number is optional until the PSTN must reach that app. The account stays disabled for sign-in. At least one Teams Phone license in the tenant turns on the voice-app services. A tenant with zero phone-system licenses will not grow a working queue out of a resource account alone.
seeds.eg: The resource account is the voice app’s identity. The number is optional until you publish it.

seeds.ex: Set business hours, holidays, a greeting you have rights to play, menu keys, directory search scope, and an operator. Directory search will find people you did not mean to publish if you leave it wide open. Each menu key needs a target: a person, a queue, another attendant, voicemail, or an external number. External targets need funding. A key that points nowhere is a silent failure with your logo on it.
seeds.eg: Hours, holidays, greeting, scoped directory, and an operator. Every key has a target.

seeds.ex: Attendant routing rings available agents together. Serial walks a list. Round robin remembers the last agent. Longest idle offers the call to the person waiting longest. Presence-based routing can skip someone who is already in a call or a meeting. Conference mode changes whether the caller sits in a conference while agents are tried. Test it with two agents, one busy, before you argue about delay.
seeds.eg: I can define the four routing methods and I will test presence with two agents.

seeds.ex: Set a timeout that a human would tolerate, and an overflow target: another queue, a person, voicemail, or an external number. Voicemail overflow needs a mailbox. External overflow, callback, and on-behalf outbound need pay-as-you-go or communications credits on the resource account. Callback is an outbound call. A greeting that promises a callback you cannot fund is a falsehood with a phone number on it.
seeds.eg: Overflow is a target I have tested. External overflow is funded.

seeds.ex: An attendant can send a key to a queue. A queue can overflow to another queue or back to an attendant. Draw it. If you cannot draw it, callers will find the loop before you do. Keep one published pilot number. Internal targets do not each need a ported number. A design that ports a number per menu key is paying carrier lead time for a diagram. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: One pilot number, a drawn tree, no loops, overflow that ends.

seeds.ex: Put service numbers on resource accounts. Do not put the main number on a receptionist’s user object. Caller ID for the queue should be chosen, not inherited from whoever built the queue. How you get the number depends on the connectivity option: Microsoft inventory, the Operator Connect carrier, or the Direct Routing carrier. Porting is a carrier project with a date, not a PowerShell metaphor. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Service numbers sit on resource accounts. Caller ID is a choice.

seeds.ti: Emergency calling is a design gate
seeds.ex: Treat emergency calling as a gate before go-live. Calling Plans in supported countries use Microsoft’s emergency service, and you still load locations. Direct Routing makes you, the SBC, and the carrier responsible for the call. Do not test by placing a real emergency call. Use the carrier’s test process.
seeds.eg: Emergency is a gate. I will not demo a bot on the emergency number.

seeds.ex: Dynamic emergency calling uses the network Teams can see. In the usual design that means trusted IPs, sites, and subnets tied to validated civic addresses. A dispatchable location is specific enough for responders. One address for five buildings is not. Trusted IPs mean ‘this client is inside our network.’ If you list the VPN concentrator, every remote user looks internal.
seeds.eg: Trusted IP, subnet, civic address. The VPN pool is not headquarters.

seeds.ti: Calling Plans versus Direct Routing emergency
seeds.ex: On Calling Plans, Microsoft’s emergency calling path is in play in supported countries, and your job is accurate locations. On Direct Routing, the emergency voice route must prefer the local SBC, and the carrier must accept the call. PIDF-LO can ride in the INVITE. If the SBC strips it, the far end may only see the trunk. An emergency calling policy controls notification and lookup.
seeds.eg: Calling Plan emergency and Direct Routing emergency are different owners. I will not copy one route onto the other.

seeds.ex: Location-based routing stops a user in a regulated site from placing or receiving PSTN through a gateway in another site. It uses the same kind of network topology as emergency location. A traveler’s laptop should not egress through another country’s SBC. Media bypass can fight this if the media path would egress in the wrong place. Read the current LBR article before you enable bypass at a regulated site.
seeds.eg: LBR keeps PSTN in-country. I will re-read it before I enable media bypass there.

seeds.ex: A Survivable Branch Appliance keeps a limited calling set for clients that can reach it when Microsoft 365 cannot. It is a Direct Routing feature. Meetings, presence, and the rest of the cloud are not the survivable set. Confirm the feature list for the firmware you run. Test a WAN cut in a window. An SBA that has never been tested is a packing slip.
seeds.eg: SBA is local PSTN survivability for Direct Routing, not a full Teams cloud.

seeds.ex: Assign the emergency calling policy that notifies the people who can meet responders. Test the notification. A policy that exists and is not assigned notifies nobody. Use the carrier’s test number or process. Do not dial the real emergency number from a lab because you were curious. Record the result: location shown, SBC used, who was notified. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I test emergency with the carrier’s process and I check that on-site notification fired.

seeds.ex: Teams-certified phones sign in as Teams users and use the Teams media stack. SIP Gateway covers a smaller set of compatible SIP and analog devices, with a smaller feature list. Check the current list before you buy. QoS for phones follows the same DSCP story, with device-specific notes in the rooms and devices articles. A phone that never registers is often identity or Conditional Access, not a codec.
seeds.eg: I buy from the current certified list, or I use SIP Gateway for the devices it actually supports.

seeds.ex: Rooms use the current Teams Rooms license. Do not borrow a user Calling Plan and hope. The room resource account must be allowed to sign in as a device. Conditional Access that assumes an interactive user will lock it out. QoS for Teams Rooms is documented separately for Windows and Android. Include the room in the same DSCP plan as the PCs, and test a call from the room, not only from a laptop. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Rooms get a room license and a Conditional Access exception you can explain.

seeds.ex: Leave analog on a certified SBC or on SIP Gateway when the device is supported. Direct Routing is the usual way to keep those devices when the humans move to Teams. A Calling Plan user license does not create an elevator phone. Test the emergency path from the analog device, including during a WAN cut if the device must keep working. An elevator that depends on a cloud sign-in is a bad surprise. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Analog stays on the SBC or SIP Gateway, with an emergency test from that device.

seeds.ex: With media bypass enabled on the gateway, media can run directly between the Teams client and the SBC instead of through Microsoft’s media processors. Signaling still uses the PSTN hubs. Microsoft does not support re-targeting that media mid-call. Bypass is a candidate when the user is on a network that can reach the SBC. A full-tunnel VPN is a poor candidate. Location-based routing may forbid the path.
seeds.eg: Bypass is media only. SIP still goes through Teams. I check LBR and the VPN first.

seeds.ex: Local media optimization uses internal and external SBC interfaces so a user inside the branch stays on the local media path. It is more specific than a single bypass checkbox. Use the current article and the SBC vendor’s build. If internal users hairpin to the public address of an SBC sitting on their own LAN, you have not finished the design. Draw the interfaces before you enable the feature. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Local media optimization is about which SBC interface the media uses. I will draw both.

seeds.ti: Common area phones, again, as devices
seeds.ex: A common-area phone is a device account plus a number plus a policy. On Direct Routing it does not need a Calling Plan. It still needs a supported phone and a network path that can reach Teams. Do not reuse a departed employee’s number by signing the phone in as that employee. That is how caller ID and voicemail become someone else’s mailbox. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: A common-area phone has its own account. I will not sign it in as a person who left.

seeds.ex: The certified list is the support boundary. AudioCodes, Ribbon, Oracle, and Cisco CUBE are families you will meet. A logo is not a certification. The software release has to be on the list. When it breaks, you call the vendor. They escalate to Microsoft if they must. Open that path with firmware, a ladder, and the paired FQDN. A homemade SBC with a clever config is an unsupported trunk. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Certification is a release on Microsoft’s list. Support starts with the vendor.

seeds.ex: AudioCodes documents Direct Routing for specific Mediant releases, often with their management tools beside the SBC. Use the document that matches the firmware. A 2019 forum post is not that document. The shared gate still applies: public certificate, verified domain, three proxies, OPTIONS, media ports, a second path, and an emergency test. Their syntax is their problem. Your job is to know which gate failed.
seeds.eg: I follow AudioCodes’ current guide for the firmware, and I still check the shared gate.

seeds.ex: Ribbon SBCs are a normal Direct Routing choice when the edition and release are certified. Answer OPTIONS on the interface Teams will actually reach. A 200 on the management port does not count. Same support rule: Ribbon first. Bring their show-tech equivalent and a SIP ladder with the Call-ID. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I confirm the Ribbon release and the interface that answers OPTIONS.

seeds.ex: Check the certified list for the Oracle software version, not the product family name. An unlisted release is an unsupported trunk no matter how complete the configuration looks. Certificate name, TLS version, and early offer still apply. Oracle’s configuration model is its own language. Translate the shared gate into that language using their current guide. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I match the Oracle release to the certified list before I praise the config.

seeds.ex: Cisco Unified Border Element on a certified IOS-XE release peers TLS with the three commercial proxies, presents a certificate whose SAN matches the paired FQDN, and has dial-peers toward Teams and toward CUCM or the carrier. Teams expects early offer. A delayed-offer trunk from CUCM pushed all the way to Teams negotiates badly. This campus does not paste a production dial-peer.
seeds.eg: CUBE is a certified SBC with dial-peers in two directions and early offer toward Teams.

seeds.ex: Collect the firmware, the paired FQDN, a ladder with Call-ID, and the OPTIONS history before you call. The vendor investigates. Microsoft may decline a case on a non-certified SBC. Keep a screenshot of the certified list from the week you bought. A 2022 PDF in the project folder is how you discover you are unsupported during the outage. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Vendor first, with firmware and a Call-ID. I keep the certified-list date.

seeds.ex: Issue a certificate whose subject or SAN contains the SBC FQDN, from a CA in the Microsoft trusted root program, with server authentication EKU. Generate the CSR on the SBC. A private lab CA is how you learn the failure, not how you run production. TLS 1.2 or newer toward the proxies. TLS 1.0 is not a compatible offer. Include the chain. An incomplete chain looks like a mysterious timeout. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Public CA, SAN matches the paired FQDN, server EKU, TLS 1.2 or newer.

seeds.ti: Names, wildcards, and the paired FQDN
seeds.ex: The name Teams checks is the FQDN you configured on the gateway. A wildcard is acceptable when it follows RFC 2818. A certificate for www.contoso.com does not cover sbc1.contoso.com. If you add a sip subdomain, verify that domain in the tenant before you pair it. DNS must resolve publicly. Split-horizon DNS that only works inside the office will not help Microsoft’s proxies. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: The certificate name, the DNS name, and the paired FQDN are the same name.

seeds.ex: Commercial clouds use sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, sip2, and sip3, on TCP 5061. IPv6 names exist on the plan page. GCC High uses sip.pstnhub.gov.teams.microsoft.us. DoD uses sip.pstnhub.dod.teams.microsoft.us. Those government clouds do not use the commercial trio. Checked 15 October 2026. The Direct Routing plan page lists commercial SBC signaling and media in 52.112.0.0/14 and 52.120.0.0/14.
seeds.eg: Three commercial proxies, government clouds have their own names, firewall the ranges.

seeds.ex: Teams sends SIP OPTIONS to the SBC. The SBC should answer while it is in service. The admin center shows SBC status from that health. This campus does not pretend to know Microsoft’s private failure counter. Repeated misses are a reason to pull the trunk from the route and look at the log. Answer on the signaling interface, not the management port. Rehearse a failure.
seeds.eg: I treat missed OPTIONS as a trunk problem and I look at the admin-center status beside the SBC log.

seeds.ex: Direct Routing lists SILK, G.711, G.722, G.729, and AMR-WB for non-bypass calls. Offer a codec both sides have. G.711 µ-law and A-law both belong if the carrier is vague. Media is SRTP. A trunk that offers only plaintext RTP is not the design. DTMF has to survive every hop or the IVR never hears 1. Test digits through the carrier, not only Teams-to-Teams. If bypass is on, do not depend on AMR-WB. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I offer G.711, I use SRTP, and I test DTMF through the carrier.

seeds.ex: In a window, break the primary path and place a call. You want to see the next proxy or the next gateway take it, and you want emergency calls to prefer the local SBC still. Write the timestamps. Certificate expiry is a failover you can predict. Put the date on a calendar and renew before Saturday morning becomes the test. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I rehearse failover and I know the certificate expiry date.

seeds.ex: Write one sentence: what you think is wrong, what you will change, what evidence would prove it. Change that thing. Collect the same Call-ID style evidence again. Then decide. A reboot plus a dial-plan edit plus a firewall change is how an outage ends with no one knowing why. The evidence pack is the Call-ID, the effective policy, the ladder, and the CQD or Call Analytics row that matches the scope.
seeds.eg: One hypothesis, one change, one evidence pack.

seeds.ex: Order the messages. INVITE, 100, 180 or 183, 200, ACK, then later BYE. 183 is early media, not an answer. 488 means the SDP was refused. 408 means something did not answer in time. 503 means the hop is refusing service. 487 often means the caller cancelled. Join on Call-ID. Two calls that start in the same second are not the same call. Read the first non-success on the hop that sent it, then stop.
seeds.eg: I read the first failing response on one Call-ID.

seeds.ex: Call Analytics shows the streams of a user’s call: jitter, loss, round-trip, and the client. Use it when one person suffered and the building did not. The Teams Communications Support Engineer role is the troubleshooting role people usually mean here. Check the current role article. A building-wide problem hunted one user at a time will take a week. Switch tools when the scope changes. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Call Analytics is one call. I will not use it to explain a subnet.

seeds.ex: CQD aggregates streams by dimensions such as subnet and user agent. Separate jitter, loss, and round-trip in your head. High jitter with DSCP 0 suggests a mark that never survived. High loss with EF still set suggests a congested or dirty link. Long RTT with almost no loss suggests distance or a hairpin. If the VPN pool is labeled headquarters, headquarters looks terrible and the real LAN is fine.
seeds.eg: I split loss, jitter, and RTT, and I trust CQD only after I trust the subnet map.

seeds.ex: Look at SBC status in the Teams admin center and at the SBC’s OPTIONS log. If TLS failed, stop. Certificate name, expiry, and chain come before regex. If OPTIONS succeed and one number fails, then you have earned the right to open the dial plan. SIP Tester language shows up in operations chatter. Use the health view and a real test call. Do not invent a hidden tester result you did not run. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I check TLS and OPTIONS before I touch a normalization rule.

seeds.ex: Silence after 200 is media ports or SRTP. 488 is codecs. A single remote user with DSCP 0 is often the VPN. A building with loss and EF intact is the link. A number that never leaves Teams is normalization or policy. A queue that does not answer is a resource account, agents, or overflow. Emergency failures are their own catalog: wrong route, missing location, stripped PIDF-LO, notification not assigned.
seeds.eg: I can sort a symptom into signaling, media, policy, or location before I pick a tool.

seeds.ex: Dynamics 365 Contact Center can stand alone or embed with Customer Service. Voice in that product uses Azure Communication Services. An auto attendant in Teams is not this product. A trial click-path is not a design: emergency calling, recording, and a busy hour are still gates. AB-250 is the exam that matches this work. MB-280 was a Sales and Customer Insights exam and it retired on 31 July 2026.
seeds.eg: Contact Center is the CCaaS. A Teams auto attendant is not. AB-250 is the exam. MB-280 is retired and was the wrong scope anyway.

seeds.ex: Voice, chat, and the other channels are the job. The study guide’s channel section is larger than the agent-and-AI section. Spend the hours there. Voice still needs numbers, a workstream, and a human path. Proactive outbound and real-time translation exist as channel behaviors. Outbound needs consent and a caller ID you mean to present. Translation does not replace a human language queue when policy requires one.
seeds.eg: Channels are the largest AB-250 slice. I will not only study Copilot.

seeds.ex: A workstream takes the item in. Classification sets language, intent, or priority. Queues hold the items. Assignment uses skills, capacity, and presence-like availability. A French billing item should not land in a general English queue because you forgot the rule. Skills must exist on the representatives, not only on a slide. If every item requires a skill nobody has, the queue never assigns.
seeds.eg: Workstream, classification, queue, assignment. Unknown intent has a human default.

seeds.ex: AB-250 calls this the representative experience: presence in the product, the session, productivity tools, and Copilot assists such as summaries. A user who can open the app and belongs to no queue is not a representative yet. Copilot that summarizes the wrong case, or quotes a stale article, is worse than silence. Connect knowledge sources you stand behind.
seeds.eg: Copilot assists the representative. It is not the route, and its sources have to be true.

seeds.ex: Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice is built with Azure Communication Services. Teams Phone extensibility lets some of those designs reuse the customer’s Teams Phone investment so the agent is not on a second phone system. The Tech Community post names that direction. Confirm the current setup guide before you promise it.
seeds.eg: Contact Center voice runs on ACS. Teams Phone extensibility is how you avoid a second phone, when the design is actually certified for it.

seeds.ex: Microsoft Learn, accessed 14 October 2026, names three models. Connect uses certified SBCs and Direct Routing. Extend uses the Teams client, Graph, and Cloud Communications APIs, with Teams Phone as the calling system. Unify is the native model. Partner text describes Unify as ACS-based applications on Teams calling infrastructure. Older decks say Power. Ask which current model the vendor holds.
seeds.eg: I use Connect, Extend, and Unify. If someone says Power, I ask which current model they mean.

seeds.ex: Teams Phone extensibility, documented for ACS and announced for Dynamics 365 Contact Center and some Unify-certified ISVs, lets the agent’s telephony be Teams Phone. The announcement named a set of vendors. That set moves. Certification is still the bar if you want the supported experience. An API existing is not a finished certification. Presence can be synced with Graph. Presence sync is not audio.
seeds.eg: Extensibility reuses Teams Phone. I want the vendor’s current certification, not only a presence sync.

seeds.ex: A calling search space is closest to a voice routing policy’s ordered usages, and it is not a one-to-one object. A translation pattern is closest to a dial-plan rule. A route pattern is closest to a voice route. There is no partition object in Teams. Pick one system to normalize numbers. Calls from people still on CUCM to people now on Teams trombone through CUBE.
seeds.eg: One normalization owner. Tromboning is temporary. Rollback keeps the old trunk.

seeds.ex: A SIP trunk through a local gateway or CUBE can carry calls between Webex Calling users and Teams users. Treat it as coexistence with one numbering plan. Two dial plans that both own a range will fail in both directions. Do not describe that trunk as a merger, and do not assume meeting interop came along for free. Write which numbers remain on Webex and for how long. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: Webex voice interop is a SIP bridge and a numbering plan, not a chat project.

seeds.ex: Leave UCCE agents on CVP and Finesse while knowledge workers move to Teams. The SBC sends contact-center numbers to CUCM and user numbers to Teams. A Teams client does not keep a CVP script in control of that agent. Test a transfer from the contact center to an expert who now lives on Teams. That expert needs Teams Phone and a number.
seeds.eg: I do not put UCCE agents on Teams and expect CVP to keep controlling them.

seeds.ex: Genesys sells Teams integrations. Ask which certification model they currently hold, because Connect, Extend, and Unify change the media path. A statement of work that says ‘certified’ and does not name the model is incomplete. Amazon Connect is often bridged with SIP through an SBC or a voice connector. Design the path and the Call-ID you will store.
seeds.eg: I ask Genesys which model, and I draw the SIP path for Amazon Connect. I store a Call-ID either way.

seeds.ex: The Calling SDK is the client for a human on a web or mobile page. Call Automation is the server API that answers, plays, recognizes, and transfers, and then receives events. A page that only uses the client SDK will not run an IVR. If your app never sees the events, the call can be up while your code is asleep. Log the event type and the call id. Event Grid is one delivery path.
seeds.eg: Call Automation is the server-side IVR. The Calling SDK is a person in the browser.

seeds.ex: ACS can be configured to call Teams users and to join Teams meetings when the interop prerequisites are met. A raw ACS identity is not a Teams user. Follow the current interop article for the resource you created. The transfer target still needs to be able to receive the call. In a Teams estate that means Teams Phone and a number when the call is PSTN. Test the transfer, not only the prompt. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: ACS does not automatically become a Teams user. I follow the interop article and I test the transfer.

seeds.ex: A small flow is answer, play, recognize DTMF or speech, then transfer or hang up. Recognize needs a timeout. Digit 0, or an equivalent, should always reach a human. Hang-up is a complete design only when the caller did not need a person. The lab on this campus is that sequence without a cloud subscription. Production adds the event subscription, the speech resource if you use one, and the queue you transfer to.
seeds.eg: Answer, play, recognize, transfer. The escape is tested every time the prompt changes.

seeds.ex: Azure AI Speech can transcribe the caller and synthesize the prompt. The language of the prompt has to match the caller or every intent becomes unknown. A custom neural voice has approval rules. Do not assume you can clone a person. Log the recognition result beside the call id. When the bot is wrong, you need the text it thought it heard, not a feeling. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I pick a voice I am allowed to use, match the language, and log what the recognizer heard.

seeds.ex: Classic topics are a menu you can test. Generative orchestration chooses a path and needs tighter bounds. Either way, ground the bot in knowledge sources you trust, and keep a human escape that does not depend on the model feeling cooperative. Do not put this bot on the emergency number. Do not make it the only target of the public number unless overflow to a queue is real and tested.
seeds.eg: The voice agent has sources I trust and an escape I tested. It does not own emergency calls.

seeds.ti: Foundry, and what not to invent
seeds.ex: Use Foundry, or the current Azure AI project experience, to evaluate prompts against questions whose answers you already know. A model change that ships to a phone number without an evaluation is an outage you chose. Do not invent unannounced voice features. A future hook in this campus is a seam you can build today: an event, an identifier, a queue overflow. It is not a rumor about a product roadmap.
seeds.eg: I evaluate the model before it touches a phone number, and I do not design around unannounced features.

seeds.ex: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. Microsoft 365 Certified: Teams Administrator Associate is earned with MS-700. The certification page, checked for this campus on 14 October 2026, does not name a successor. Third-party claims that an MS-220 collaboration exam replaced it are not what Learn showed on that date.
seeds.eg: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement.

seeds.ti: Learning paths that match the job
seeds.ex: Follow the same order as this campus: tenant and licenses, network, connectivity, routing, voice apps, emergency, SBC, then the contact center. Microsoft Learn modules exist for Teams Phone, Direct Routing, QoS, and the AB-250 course family. Use them as the official wording beside these notes. When a module and this page disagree, the module accessed the week you need it wins.
seeds.eg: I study foundations, then the phone system, then the contact center. I re-read Learn when I am about to change production.

seeds.ex: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. Also on the board: MS-900 retired 31 March 2026, AI-900 retired 30 June 2026, AB-250’s public beta discount ran through 18 June 2026, and SC-900’s English update is scheduled for 21 October 2026.
seeds.eg: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta.

seeds.ti: How to use the readiness map
seeds.ex: Rate yourself 0 to 3 on the live exams. Anything under 2 on MS-700, AB-250, AZ-900, or SC-900 is a study target, not a personality result. AB-210 is a target only if the job is Sales. MB-280, MS-900, and AI-900 are not targets. The rating stays in this browser. It is not an account and not a certificate. Book the exam only after you re-open the study guide. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: A readiness score is mine, in this browser, and the study guide still wins.

seeds.ti: Voice is not a closed box
seeds.ex: Teams Phone gets a number to a person or a voice app. Around that call sit Cloud Voicemail, emergency location, a certified recorder, a queue’s interval stats, a CRM case, and sometimes a bot. Each of those is a sister system with its own configuration and its own failure. This track is the map of those systems. It does not replace the earlier tracks. If the trunk is down, the CRM pop is not the lead.
seeds.eg: I can name the sister system and the identifier that joins it to the call.

seeds.ex: Each term has a plain definition, a reason it matters, a configuration hint, and a fault you should recognize. Filter by track. If a definition and a vendor blog disagree, open the source link. The access date is 14 October 2026. Flashcards are the same facts in recall form. Do not treat a card you flipped once as evidence you can operate the system. The lab is that evidence. Checked 2026-10-14.
seeds.eg: I can define the term, the fault, and the document I would open.

seeds.ex: The map puts Entra ID and Cloud Voicemail beside Teams Phone, the dial plan in front of routing, the SBC between Teams and the carrier, and emergency location on that SBC path. Attendants, Dynamics, ACS, Copilot Studio, recording, WFM, Power BI, and the CRM sit on named edges. Click a node in the map view.
seeds.eg: I can draw Teams, the SBC, the carrier, and the six sister systems without notes.

seeds.ex: Convenience recording is started by a licensed user and stored with the meeting. Compliance recording is a third-party bot invited by policy into new calls, meetings, and events. Microsoft’s comparison, accessed 14 October 2026, says notification is enforced, participant consent is not the compliance control, and audio-only is not the compliance mode. Listed media is voice, video, and screen share.
seeds.eg: Compliance recording is a partner bot, a policy, and an application instance. Users do not start it. I test a new call.

seeds.ex: Workforce management consumes offered, answered, abandoned, and handle time from the contact center or the queue, in the same interval the schedule uses. Erlang C is a teaching model of how many people must be available. Shrinkage is the fraction of paid time that is not available. Roster is larger than the Erlang number. Occupancy is handle time over handle time plus ready time.
seeds.eg: I staff from queue intervals, Erlang C, and an explicit shrinkage. I do not staff from Call Analytics.

seeds.ti: E911 as a system of record
seeds.ex: Keep one subnet list. Emergency location, location-based routing, and the CQD building map should read it. Three spreadsheets will drift, and then E911 says London, CQD says VPN, and LBR says Manchester. Configuration is the topology plus the emergency policy plus the route plus the carrier test. Troubleshooting starts with ‘which subnet did the client present,’ not with the SBC firmware.
seeds.eg: One subnet list feeds emergency location, LBR, and CQD. I can say which consumer is wrong when they disagree.

seeds.ex: Call Analytics is one call. CQD is the estate. Contact-center analytics are the queue: service level, abandon, handle time. Power BI can sit on CQD data, and contact-center implementations often surface supervisor numbers in Power BI. The report inherits a bad subnet map and a bad abandon rule. Troubleshooting: if leadership sees a red headquarters, check the VPN labeling before you buy circuits.
seeds.eg: Power BI comes after the grain is right. I will not show a VPN pool as headquarters.

seeds.ex: Screen pop is a contact-center or middleware behavior. It looks up a contact from the caller number. That number has to be E.164 after normalization. Store the SIP Call-ID, the queue, and the agent on the timeline. A note that says ‘called customer’ cannot be audited. Troubleshooting: the wrong contact pops when a trunk prefix is still on the number, or when one human has two caller IDs.
seeds.eg: Screen pop needs E.164 and should write the Call-ID. Teams alone does not open the case.

seeds.ex: Put the agent in front of a queue only when knowledge sources are grounded, the escape digit works, and unknown intent reaches a human. Generative orchestration is less predictable than classic topics. Evaluate prompt changes before they are on a public number. Foundry is the evaluation place, not a second SBC. Troubleshooting: if callers loop, the recognize step has no escape or the fallback topic is empty.
seeds.eg: The agent has a tested escape and a staffed overflow. It is not the emergency route.

seeds.ex: Recording regulated calls implies a certified recorder, an application instance, a policy, the users in scope, and a Call-ID. A CRM pop implies E.164 and middleware. Staffing implies queue intervals and shrinkage. WAN survival implies Direct Routing and an SBA. A bad building implies CQD and the subnet map. A bot implies an escape and a queue. The integration-map lab asks you to pick the goal and read that list.
seeds.eg: I start from the goal and list the systems, including the identifier.

seeds.ex: The bridge is a certified SBC, often CUBE, with one normalization owner, a written number range, and a rollback that still has the old route. Identity is not shared automatically between CUCM and Entra. Presence is not a call route. Chat interop is not voice. Genesys needs a named Connect, Extend, or Unify certification. Amazon Connect needs a drawn SIP path.
seeds.eg: A cross-platform voice bridge is an SBC, one normalizer, written ranges, and a rollback.

seeds.ex: Leave these seams: store the Call-ID on the CRM timeline, assign the recording policy in the same change as the number, let overflow become a bot without a new public number, keep one subnet list, route by SBC FQDN rather than a copied proxy IP, make queue intervals exportable to WFM, test the human escape, and monitor certificate expiry. None of these require an unannounced feature.
seeds.eg: I can name the seams I am leaving, and the failure if I skip one. I am not promising an unannounced product.

seeds.ex: Write the change as a list: tenant, license, route, emergency subnet, recording policy, queue or workstream, CRM field, and the rollback. Do the lab version first. Read effective policy after each grant. Acquire resource-account licenses even when the price is zero. Include the certificate expiry and the holiday calendar if the change touches an attendant. Include shrinkage if the change adds a queue.
seeds.eg: My change list names the sisters, not only the SBC.

seeds.ex: Name the boundary: Teams and SBC, SBC and carrier, Teams and recorder, queue and WFM, number and CRM. Collect the join key on both sides before anyone changes anything. Call-ID for SIP. E.164 for the CRM. Interval timestamp for WFM. Subnet for E911 and CQD. One change, on the side the evidence names. Vendor-first if it is the SBC. Partner-first if it is the recorder.
seeds.eg: I name the boundary and the join key before I ask a vendor to change anything.

seeds.ex: Wikipedia’s page for computer telephony integration says computer-telephony integration, also called computer–telephone integration or CTI, is a general term for technologies that coordinate interactions between telephones and computers. The following sentence on that page is marked citation needed. This room stops at the sourced sentence. Dynamics 365 and Salesforce each publish a specific bridge.
seeds.eg: CTI names the coordination. The vendor page names the product.

seeds.ex: The introduction to the voice channel applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center embedded, Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone, and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. It says representatives receive and make PSTN calls through a native calling experience in Dynamics 365, and that the voice channel is built on Azure Communication Services.
seeds.eg: The voice channel is ACS calling inside Dynamics, routed like the other channels.

seeds.ti: Teams Phone into the voice channel
seeds.ex: The page Configure Teams Phone in the voice channel says the PSTN connectivity is a Teams Calling Plan, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing. For a Teams Calling Plan, that page says service numbers only are supported. It also lists Enterprise Voice, outbound-calling prerequisites, and a licensing guide. This room does not copy SKU names from the licensing guide.
seeds.eg: Teams can carry the number. A Calling Plan here is service numbers only.

seeds.ti: The resource account and the number
seeds.ex: The same page shows Connect-MicrosoftTeams, then New-CsOnlineApplicationInstance, then Set-CsOnlineApplicationInstance and Sync-CsOnlineApplicationInstance. Those last two examples include an ApplicationId and the organization’s Azure Communication Services resource ID. Copy both from the current page. This room does not ask you to memorize the identifier.
seeds.eg: I sync the Teams service number, and the representative answers in Copilot Service workspace.

seeds.ti: Salesforce Voice and Partner Contact Center
seeds.ex: The help page opened for this room is titled Connect Voice from a Partner Contact Center. It says Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers, formerly Service Cloud Voice, is now part of Partner Contact Center, and that you may still see the older name. Its learning map lists the Telephony Integration REST API, the Voice Toolkit API, and Lambda functions for Amazon Connect under Develop.
seeds.eg: Service Cloud Voice is now Salesforce Voice, and the help page places it in Partner Contact Center.

seeds.ex: The learning map on Connect Voice from a Partner Contact Center lists separate setup paths: Partner Contact Center with Amazon Connect, Partner Contact Center Voice, and Partner Contact Center with Amazon Connect as bring your own. It also lists supervisor listen-in and barge-in, linking calls with customer contact records, and the Telephony Integration REST API and Voice Toolkit API under Develop.
seeds.eg: I can point at which Salesforce telephony path the learning map names.

seeds.ex: Microsoft’s Teams contact-center article describes three provider models. Extend uses the Teams client as the calling endpoint. The Dynamics Teams Phone page, which is a different article, says the representative receives the Teams-number call in the Copilot Service workspace app. Those are different desktops. Do not describe the Dynamics workspace as the Extend client.
seeds.eg: I name the desktop that answers, and the identifier that joins the call to the record.

seeds.ex: Each later room uses a page this lab opened in October 2026. The product name is the name printed on that page. If two pages use two names, both names stay, with the page each one came from. Bars in this track are equal on purpose. Length is not a rank, a price, or a market share. Words such as a superlative for quality, a prize, or a promise of no effort are not used here, even when a vendor page uses them.
seeds.eg: I can cite the page, and I will not rank the vendors.

seeds.ex: The Dynamics voice-channel page says the channel provides native PSTN calling in Dynamics 365, is built on Azure Communication Services, and routes calls with unified routing. The Teams Phone page says a Teams number used with Contact Center is a Calling Plan service number, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing, and that the representative is notified in Copilot Service workspace.
seeds.eg: I can say which Microsoft article I am quoting before I name a model.

seeds.ex: That guide says Amazon Connect Customer is the current name for the product previously called Amazon Connect. It says Amazon Connect is now a set of agentic AI solutions for different business functions, and that this guide covers Amazon Connect Customer. This room uses that distinction and does not describe the other functions. The page says agents spend time on voice, chat, SMS, or other channels.
seeds.eg: The guide I opened calls the contact-center product Amazon Connect Customer.

seeds.ti: CCAI Platform and the GECX rename
seeds.ex: The docs page opened for this room is titled Contact Center AI Platform. It says CCAI Platform is built natively on Google Cloud, uses other Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience products, and is purpose-built to work alongside CRMs.
seeds.eg: The docs page still says Contact Center AI Platform. The change log records the GECX rename.

seeds.ex: Dynamics, on the voice-channel page: native PSTN calling in Dynamics, built on Azure Communication Services, routed with unified routing, with customer and case lookup in the capabilities table. Teams providers, on the contact-center page: Unify, Extend, or Connect, as the previous room states.
seeds.eg: I can fill the table from the pages and leave the score column off.

seeds.ti: What these pages do not decide
seeds.ex: These pages do not state a price figure this room can repeat. Amazon’s guide says you pay only for what you use and links pricing. No amount is copied. They do not state market share. They do not rank the products. The Teams article links a certified-solutions list and a list of providers in the certification process. This track does not paste either list.
seeds.eg: I can say what this comparison refuses to decide.

seeds.ex: The unified-routing overview applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center embedded, Contact Center standalone, and Customer Service. It says unified routing has two stages. In classification, rules and machine-learning models can add information on the work item. In assignment, requests are prioritized and then assigned using the nature of the work, related entities, skills, and the current availability and workload.
seeds.eg: Classification adds information. Assignment uses it. They are not the same stage.

seeds.ex: The workstreams page says a workstream is a container to enrich, route, and assign work items. Types are Messaging, Record, and Voice. Voice routes calls to support numbers. In the create dialog, Push sends the work with a message alert, and Pick waits until someone takes it from Open work items. For voice, push mode only is available, and the work distribution mode cannot be edited later.
seeds.eg: A voice workstream is push only. I will not edit that mode later, because the page says I cannot.

seeds.ti: Highest capacity, round robin, least active
seeds.ex: Highest capacity assigns to the representative with the highest available capacity who has the skills from classification and an allowed presence. If more than one has the same capacity, the page says round-robin order breaks the tie. Exact match filters on an exact skill match and then orders by available capacity. Closest match orders by closest match rather than by available capacity.
seeds.eg: I can name which assignment method the queue uses, and I will not use it to rank employees.

seeds.ex: The forecasting overview says a forecast estimates volume and average handle time by channel and queue. Volume excludes conversations that AI agents handle with no representative joining. Forecasting is the first stage. Capacity planning uses the default forecast snapshot to calculate staffing requirements. Scheduling turns those requirements into shifts.
seeds.eg: Forecast volume and handle time, then capacity, then shifts. The short-term horizon on the page is up to 42 days.

seeds.ex: The quality and coaching page applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center only. An evaluation plan sets the criteria, which conversations, the timing, and the actions. Frequency is In real time, during the conversation, or On conversation close, after it ends. Conditions pick the queue or workstream. Sampling is a percentage.
seeds.eg: An indicator scores. A guardrail flags a required or prohibited behavior. Neither one is an employment decision.

seeds.ex: The Configure Teams Phone in the voice channel page says that when call recording is enabled, an announcement plays to notify participants. The voice-channel capabilities table also lists transcription and recording, and supervisor record and manage. That is the Dynamics side.
seeds.eg: I will check the Dynamics announcement and the Teams recording policy as two controls.

seeds.ex: If the work never reaches a queue, read classification and the route-to-queue rules, then the fallback queue. If it reaches the queue and the wrong person gets it, read the assignment method, presence, capacity, and skills. If the queue is staffed for the wrong interval, read the forecast scenario type before you edit the assignment method.
seeds.eg: I name the control that failed before I change a different one.

docs.ex: Track t01 is Foundations. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

A Microsoft 365 tenant holds Entra ID, the license pool, Teams policies, and the verified domains. Direct Routing will only pair an SBC FQDN that belongs to one of those verified domains. The default onmicrosoft.com domain is not eligible. Before you discuss codecs, say which tenant you are in and whether the users are homed online. Direct Routing is not supported in Islands mode.
docs.eg: Name the tenant, the verified domain, and that onmicrosoft.com cannot be the SBC name.

docs.ti: Entra ID accounts voice will use
docs.ex: Humans, rooms, and resource accounts are Entra objects. Resource accounts are disabled for sign-in on purpose. They represent an auto attendant or a call queue. They are not a shared mailbox someone should open in Outlook as their daily driver. Create the object, license it, then grant voice policy. Creating a resource account takes a Teams administrator role and the User Administrator role.
docs.eg: Resource accounts do not sign in. Humans and rooms do.

docs.ex: Teams Administrator, Teams Telephony Administrator, and Teams Communications Administrator cover different slices of calling and meetings. Support Engineer and Support Specialist are troubleshooting roles, useful for Call Analytics, and the wrong tool for building a dial plan. Use the smallest role that can do the change. Keep named accounts. Conditional Access belongs on those admin accounts.
docs.eg: I will use a telephony or Teams admin role, not a shared global admin.

docs.ex: Numbers, voice routing, attendants, and queues are Teams admin center work, with PowerShell beside them. Licenses, including the Teams Phone Resource Account license, are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Emergency addresses and network topology sit with the voice configuration, not with a random SharePoint site. When the portal and the shell disagree, read the user with Get-CsOnlineUser.
docs.eg: Licenses in one center, voice objects in the other, effective policy from the shell.

docs.ex: Cloud Voicemail deposits the message in the user’s Exchange mailbox. No mailbox, no deposit. Overflow from a queue to voicemail fails the same way if the account that should receive the message has nowhere to put it. Debug voicemail only after the call has actually reached the voicemail path. If the ladder dies at the carrier, the mailbox is innocent.
docs.eg: Cloud Voicemail needs a mailbox. The SBC cannot store the message for you.

docs.ex: Direct Routing expects the user to be homed in Microsoft 365. Islands mode is explicitly unsupported for Direct Routing. Those are registrar and coexistence facts, not SBC opinions. Read the user before you assign a voice routing policy. If the pilot group is a mix of online users and leftover coexistence modes, you will debug one trunk twice and learn nothing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Direct Routing users are homed online, and they are not in Islands mode.

docs.ex: Track t02 is Licensing. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

A person who places or receives PSTN calls needs Teams and Teams Phone, unless a bundle already includes that capability. Confirm the bundle on the licensing page, because names move. A Calling Plan, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing is the connectivity choice on top.
docs.eg: Teams Phone is not a carrier. Name the connectivity option separately.

docs.ex: Calling Plans make Microsoft the carrier. You pick a flavor that matches how the user dials, and you can only buy it where Microsoft sells it. Pay-as-you-go is also the funding pattern, with communications credits, for some voice-app outbound calls. A user in a country without Calling Plans needs Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing. Assigning a SKU that cannot be used is not a routing problem.
docs.eg: Calling Plans are Microsoft as the carrier, sold only in some countries, in three usual flavors.

docs.ex: Teams Premium adds meeting and related features. It does not replace Teams Phone, a Calling Plan, Audio Conferencing, or a resource-account license. If a proposal removes Calling Plans because Premium was purchased, the proposal is wrong. Say that out loud in the interview. Then go back to the connectivity option the users actually need. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Teams Premium does not include a phone system or a carrier.

docs.ex: Each auto attendant or call queue that answers needs a resource account with a Microsoft Teams Phone Resource Account license, even when you do not assign a phone number. Tenants with Teams Phone get a zero-cost allotment, and you still have to acquire those licenses. Do not assign Teams Phone Standard to a resource account.
docs.eg: Resource accounts get the Teams Phone Resource Account license, not Teams Phone Standard.

docs.ti: Rooms, common area, and shared calling
docs.ex: A common-area phone on Direct Routing does not need a Calling Plan. Teams Rooms use the current room SKU, not a borrowed user license. Shared Calling lets people place outbound calls through a resource account’s number, and it has its own funding rules. Read the current page for the pattern you are about to promise. Room names change.
docs.eg: A Direct Routing common-area phone does not need a Calling Plan. A room has its own SKU.

docs.ti: A license set you can defend
docs.ex: Walk the picker in this order: does the person need PSTN, who is the carrier, do meetings need a dial-in number, is there a room, is there a voice app, does that app dial out. Audio Conferencing is the meeting dial-in. It is not implied by Teams Phone. End with the sentence that Teams Premium changed none of those answers.
docs.eg: I separate Teams Phone, the carrier, Audio Conferencing, the resource account, and Premium.

docs.ex: Track t03 is PowerShell and admin. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Install the MicrosoftTeams module and connect it to the tenant you named in the foundations track. Confirm you are not in production. Cmdlet parameters move between module versions, so Get-Help in the version you are about to run beats a blog post. Compliance recording policies are created and granted in this module. If you only learn the portal, you cannot finish a recorder design. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I connect the MicrosoftTeams module to a named tenant and read help before I change anything.

docs.ex: A dial plan holds normalization rules. A voice route holds a pattern and gateways. A PSTN usage is a name that ties routes to a policy. A voice routing policy is the ordered list of usages you grant to a user. A PSTN gateway is the paired SBC. Application instances show up twice in real designs: resource accounts for voice apps, and bots for compliance recording.
docs.eg: Usage, route, policy, gateway. The policy is what the user has. The route is what the pattern does.

docs.ex: New-CsOnlineVoiceRoute creates a route. Set-CsOnlinePstnUsage maintains the usage list. Grant-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy assigns a policy to a user. Grant-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy assigns a recorder policy. None of those verbs is a synonym. Read with Get- before you Set- or Grant-. Then read again. The second read is the evidence pack, not a personality trait. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Grant assigns to a user. Set changes an object. I read both times.

docs.ti: Reading a user before you change one
docs.ex: Get-CsOnlineUser shows voice policy, dial plan, and number fields. Look at the effective values. A group grant can beat the direct assignment you remember from last quarter. Test the call as that user, from the client they actually use. A browser join and a certified phone do not take the same media path, and QoS will not treat them the same either. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I read the effective policy with Get-CsOnlineUser before I edit anything.

docs.ti: When the portal and the shell disagree
docs.ex: If the Teams admin center shows a policy and the shell shows another, believe the shell long enough to place a test call, then refresh both. Replication delay is real. An hour of firmware changes during that delay is not. Write down the time, the cmdlet, and the values. That note is the evidence pack. It is also how you avoid changing three systems because one screen was stale. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I will trust a fresh Get- over a stale toast, then place one test call.

docs.ex: Pair a lab SBC to a lab domain. Use obviously fake names. Contoso and 555 numbers exist so practice does not point at a real directory. Do not find-and-replace a lab script onto production without reading every name. Production changes get one hypothesis, a rollback, and a window. The lab is where you learn that a private CA will not satisfy Direct Routing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I will not discover certificate behavior on the company trunk.

docs.ex: Track t04 is Network and QoS. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Microsoft’s QoS and network articles tell you to keep the path short: on the order of three to five hops from the client to your edge, and a short path from the ISP to Microsoft. Proxies in the media path are a known way to damage calls. ExpressRoute is not required. Draw the path a branch actually uses. If that branch backhauls across a continent to egress, you already know why RTT is high.
docs.eg: Local egress, no media proxy, ExpressRoute not required.

docs.ex: The QoS article’s initial ranges are audio UDP or TCP 50000–50019 at DSCP 46 EF, video 50020–50039 at 34 AF41, sharing 50040–50059 at 18 AF21, and calling and meeting signaling 50070–50089 at 40 CS5. Signaling ports are not configurable. Browser joins do not use those fixed ranges. Mac and mobile hard-code audio as EF.
docs.eg: Audio is 46 on ports 50000 to 50019. I can place the other three without a card.

docs.ex: Microsoft recommends that you avoid real-time media on a VPN. QoS inside the tunnel only prioritizes traffic inside a path that is already longer. Split tunnel is the usual way to let media go direct while other traffic stays on the VPN. A VPN pool labeled as headquarters will make CQD accuse the wrong building and can make dynamic emergency calling report the wrong place.
docs.eg: I keep real-time media off the full-tunnel VPN, and I do not label the VPN pool as HQ.

docs.ex: G.711 at 20 milliseconds is 160 bytes of payload. Add 40 bytes of IP, UDP, and RTP and the call is 80 kbit/s per direction at layer 3. Add an 18-byte Ethernet header and it is 87.2 kbit/s. G.729 at the same interval is 20 bytes of payload, 24 kbit/s at layer 3. Silence suppression and a different packet interval change the average.
docs.eg: G.711 at 20 ms is 80 kbit/s at layer 3 and 87.2 with a typical Ethernet header.

docs.ex: Capture at the network egress, not only on the PC. You want the DSCP value on the wire after the VPN, the switch, and the router. Port mirroring is the usual way. If audio ports 50000–50019 leave the building marked 0, the client policy missed or a device rewrote the mark. Fix that before you argue about codecs. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I capture at the egress and show DSCP 46 still on the audio ports.

docs.ex: Teams is designed to work over the internet with local egress. If your organization also has ExpressRoute, follow the current network documentation for which traffic belongs there. Do not assume media is automatically better on the private path. QoS still has to be consistent on whatever path you chose. A private path with no marks and extra distance is a slower best-effort network. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Teams does not require ExpressRoute. Local internet egress is the normal plan.

docs.ex: Track t05 is PSTN connectivity. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

docs.ti: Four ways to reach the PSTN
docs.ex: The four options on the connectivity page are Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. The others use a partner or your SBC. One tenant may use all four for different people. Operator Connect for India is its own plan because the regulatory problem is different. Do not hide an India office inside a UK SBC and call it Operator Connect.
docs.eg: Four options. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. Mixing them in one tenant is allowed.

docs.ex: You assign the plan, you receive numbers from Microsoft, and emergency calling in supported countries is part of that service. You still configure emergency locations. You do not pair an SBC for those users. If a Calling Plan user also matches a Direct Routing voice route, you may send their calls onto your SBC by accident. The policy has to match the license. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Calling Plan users should not inherit a Direct Routing route by accident.

docs.ex: The operator is enabled in the tenant and assigns numbers. You need Teams Phone. You do not need a Microsoft Calling Plan, and you do not run the SBC. India has a separate operator plan. Ask the operator which numbers are service numbers for attendants and which are user numbers. A user number that walks out the door with an employee is a publishing problem. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Operator Connect is Teams Phone plus a certified carrier. I do not also build an SBC for those same numbers.

docs.ex: Teams Phone Mobile uses a certified mobile operator. The user’s SIM number is assigned as their Teams number. They need Teams Phone. They do not need a separate Calling Plan for that path. Do not put the main queue on someone’s SIM. When that person leaves, the number leaves. CRM matching also fails if the same human presents two caller IDs. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Teams Phone Mobile makes the SIM number the Teams number. I would not put a queue on it.

docs.ex: You pair an SBC FQDN on a verified domain, present a public certificate, signal TLS to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com and its sip2 and sip3 partners on port 5061, and allow media UDP 3478–3481 and 49152–53247. Firewall rules must allow the published IP ranges, not only today’s DNS answer. GCC High and DoD use different proxy names. Users need Teams and Teams Phone, homed online, not in Islands mode.
docs.eg: 5061 to the three commercial proxies, media on those UDP ranges, certificate name matches the FQDN, user has a route.

docs.ex: Write a table: population, connectivity, policy, who operates the trunk. A contact center on Direct Routing and a headquarters on Operator Connect is a normal tenant, not a compromise. The failure mode is a single voice routing policy granted to everyone. Mobile users then hairpin through an SBC they should never touch, or Calling Plan emergency calls leave the country. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I mix options on purpose, with a policy per population.

docs.ex: Track t06 is Routing and dial plans. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

The person dials 020 7555 4010 or 425 555 0100. The first matching normalization rule rewrites it. Later rules do not run. The voice route then sees the result, usually E.164. Put emergency short codes above any catch-all. A rule that turns every three-digit string into an extension will eat 999. Test the raw digits and the normalized form. The route is not wrong just because you typed the raw digits into it.
docs.eg: First matching normalization rule wins. I test the route with the normalized number.

docs.ex: Tenant dial plans hold the rules. Grant the plan to the users it describes. A user with a specific plan will not pick up your edit to the global plan. Keep rules anchored. A pattern without an end anchor will match a prefix of a longer number and translate the wrong thing. The lab on this campus is a teaching matcher with the same first-match idea, not the Microsoft service. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Specific rules first, grant the plan to the user, test as that user.

docs.ex: PSTN usages are names. Voice routes attach to them. The user’s voice routing policy lists the usages in order. Teams walks that order. This campus’s matcher does the same and says so on the lab. Give a branch a policy whose usages stop at national. Give headquarters a policy that continues to international. Do not share one policy and hope the route patterns save you. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: The usage is the permission. The policy is the ordered list of permissions on the user.

docs.ex: Anchor the pattern to the normalized number. List gateways with priorities. In this campus, priority 1 is tried first. Confirm the current article before you depend on a production tie-break. A second gateway that has never carried a call is a drawing. Unassigned numbers you own should be treated on purpose, usually toward an attendant. A ported block with fifty silent numbers looks like an outage.
docs.eg: The voice route is a regex and a gateway list. I rehearse failover.

docs.ex: A London user dials a UK national number. Their dial plan emits +44. Their policy lists emergency, then UK national, then international. The UK route matches +44 and prefers sbc-lon, with sbc-man as priority 2. A Manchester-only policy has no international usage, so a US number fails closed.
docs.eg: I can walk one number through normalize, usage, route, and gateway.

docs.ti: Islands mode and other hard stops
docs.ex: Direct Routing is not supported in Islands mode. An SBC FQDN on onmicrosoft.com is not supported. A private CA is not a production certificate. AMR-WB is not a bypass codec.
