Media cannot be re-targeted mid-call. Memorize the hard stops. They save you from debugging a dial plan that was never going to run. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I list the hard stops before I tune a regex.

docs.ex: Track t07 is Attendants and queues. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Create the resource account, assign the Teams Phone Resource Account license, and attach it to the attendant or queue. A phone number is optional until the PSTN must reach that app. The account stays disabled for sign-in. At least one Teams Phone license in the tenant turns on the voice-app services. A tenant with zero phone-system licenses will not grow a working queue out of a resource account alone.
docs.eg: The resource account is the voice app’s identity. The number is optional until you publish it.

docs.ex: Set business hours, holidays, a greeting you have rights to play, menu keys, directory search scope, and an operator. Directory search will find people you did not mean to publish if you leave it wide open. Each menu key needs a target: a person, a queue, another attendant, voicemail, or an external number. External targets need funding. A key that points nowhere is a silent failure with your logo on it.
docs.eg: Hours, holidays, greeting, scoped directory, and an operator. Every key has a target.

docs.ex: Attendant routing rings available agents together. Serial walks a list. Round robin remembers the last agent. Longest idle offers the call to the person waiting longest. Presence-based routing can skip someone who is already in a call or a meeting. Conference mode changes whether the caller sits in a conference while agents are tried. Test it with two agents, one busy, before you argue about delay.
docs.eg: I can define the four routing methods and I will test presence with two agents.

docs.ex: Set a timeout that a human would tolerate, and an overflow target: another queue, a person, voicemail, or an external number. Voicemail overflow needs a mailbox. External overflow, callback, and on-behalf outbound need pay-as-you-go or communications credits on the resource account. Callback is an outbound call. A greeting that promises a callback you cannot fund is a falsehood with a phone number on it.
docs.eg: Overflow is a target I have tested. External overflow is funded.

docs.ex: An attendant can send a key to a queue. A queue can overflow to another queue or back to an attendant. Draw it. If you cannot draw it, callers will find the loop before you do. Keep one published pilot number. Internal targets do not each need a ported number. A design that ports a number per menu key is paying carrier lead time for a diagram. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: One pilot number, a drawn tree, no loops, overflow that ends.

docs.ex: Put service numbers on resource accounts. Do not put the main number on a receptionist’s user object. Caller ID for the queue should be chosen, not inherited from whoever built the queue. How you get the number depends on the connectivity option: Microsoft inventory, the Operator Connect carrier, or the Direct Routing carrier. Porting is a carrier project with a date, not a PowerShell metaphor. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Service numbers sit on resource accounts. Caller ID is a choice.

docs.ex: Track t08 is Emergency, LBR, survivability. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

docs.ti: Emergency calling is a design gate
docs.ex: Treat emergency calling as a gate before go-live. Calling Plans in supported countries use Microsoft’s emergency service, and you still load locations. Direct Routing makes you, the SBC, and the carrier responsible for the call. Do not test by placing a real emergency call. Use the carrier’s test process.
docs.eg: Emergency is a gate. I will not demo a bot on the emergency number.

docs.ex: Dynamic emergency calling uses the network Teams can see. In the usual design that means trusted IPs, sites, and subnets tied to validated civic addresses. A dispatchable location is specific enough for responders. One address for five buildings is not. Trusted IPs mean ‘this client is inside our network.’ If you list the VPN concentrator, every remote user looks internal.
docs.eg: Trusted IP, subnet, civic address. The VPN pool is not headquarters.

docs.ti: Calling Plans versus Direct Routing emergency
docs.ex: On Calling Plans, Microsoft’s emergency calling path is in play in supported countries, and your job is accurate locations. On Direct Routing, the emergency voice route must prefer the local SBC, and the carrier must accept the call. PIDF-LO can ride in the INVITE. If the SBC strips it, the far end may only see the trunk. An emergency calling policy controls notification and lookup.
docs.eg: Calling Plan emergency and Direct Routing emergency are different owners. I will not copy one route onto the other.

docs.ex: Location-based routing stops a user in a regulated site from placing or receiving PSTN through a gateway in another site. It uses the same kind of network topology as emergency location. A traveler’s laptop should not egress through another country’s SBC. Media bypass can fight this if the media path would egress in the wrong place. Read the current LBR article before you enable bypass at a regulated site.
docs.eg: LBR keeps PSTN in-country. I will re-read it before I enable media bypass there.

docs.ex: A Survivable Branch Appliance keeps a limited calling set for clients that can reach it when Microsoft 365 cannot. It is a Direct Routing feature. Meetings, presence, and the rest of the cloud are not the survivable set. Confirm the feature list for the firmware you run. Test a WAN cut in a window. An SBA that has never been tested is a packing slip.
docs.eg: SBA is local PSTN survivability for Direct Routing, not a full Teams cloud.

docs.ex: Assign the emergency calling policy that notifies the people who can meet responders. Test the notification. A policy that exists and is not assigned notifies nobody. Use the carrier’s test number or process. Do not dial the real emergency number from a lab because you were curious. Record the result: location shown, SBC used, who was notified. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I test emergency with the carrier’s process and I check that on-site notification fired.

docs.ex: Track t09 is Devices and media. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Teams-certified phones sign in as Teams users and use the Teams media stack. SIP Gateway covers a smaller set of compatible SIP and analog devices, with a smaller feature list. Check the current list before you buy. QoS for phones follows the same DSCP story, with device-specific notes in the rooms and devices articles. A phone that never registers is often identity or Conditional Access, not a codec.
docs.eg: I buy from the current certified list, or I use SIP Gateway for the devices it actually supports.

docs.ex: Rooms use the current Teams Rooms license. Do not borrow a user Calling Plan and hope. The room resource account must be allowed to sign in as a device. Conditional Access that assumes an interactive user will lock it out. QoS for Teams Rooms is documented separately for Windows and Android. Include the room in the same DSCP plan as the PCs, and test a call from the room, not only from a laptop. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Rooms get a room license and a Conditional Access exception you can explain.

docs.ex: Leave analog on a certified SBC or on SIP Gateway when the device is supported. Direct Routing is the usual way to keep those devices when the humans move to Teams. A Calling Plan user license does not create an elevator phone. Test the emergency path from the analog device, including during a WAN cut if the device must keep working. An elevator that depends on a cloud sign-in is a bad surprise. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Analog stays on the SBC or SIP Gateway, with an emergency test from that device.

docs.ex: With media bypass enabled on the gateway, media can run directly between the Teams client and the SBC instead of through Microsoft’s media processors. Signaling still uses the PSTN hubs. Microsoft does not support re-targeting that media mid-call. Bypass is a candidate when the user is on a network that can reach the SBC. A full-tunnel VPN is a poor candidate. Location-based routing may forbid the path.
docs.eg: Bypass is media only. SIP still goes through Teams. I check LBR and the VPN first.

docs.ex: Local media optimization uses internal and external SBC interfaces so a user inside the branch stays on the local media path. It is more specific than a single bypass checkbox. Use the current article and the SBC vendor’s build. If internal users hairpin to the public address of an SBC sitting on their own LAN, you have not finished the design. Draw the interfaces before you enable the feature. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Local media optimization is about which SBC interface the media uses. I will draw both.

docs.ti: Common area phones, again, as devices
docs.ex: A common-area phone is a device account plus a number plus a policy. On Direct Routing it does not need a Calling Plan. It still needs a supported phone and a network path that can reach Teams. Do not reuse a departed employee’s number by signing the phone in as that employee. That is how caller ID and voicemail become someone else’s mailbox. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: A common-area phone has its own account. I will not sign it in as a person who left.

docs.ex: Track t10 is Session border controllers. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

The certified list is the support boundary. AudioCodes, Ribbon, Oracle, and Cisco CUBE are families you will meet. A logo is not a certification. The software release has to be on the list. When it breaks, you call the vendor. They escalate to Microsoft if they must. Open that path with firmware, a ladder, and the paired FQDN. A homemade SBC with a clever config is an unsupported trunk. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Certification is a release on Microsoft’s list. Support starts with the vendor.

docs.ex: AudioCodes documents Direct Routing for specific Mediant releases, often with their management tools beside the SBC. Use the document that matches the firmware. A 2019 forum post is not that document. The shared gate still applies: public certificate, verified domain, three proxies, OPTIONS, media ports, a second path, and an emergency test. Their syntax is their problem. Your job is to know which gate failed.
docs.eg: I follow AudioCodes’ current guide for the firmware, and I still check the shared gate.

docs.ex: Ribbon SBCs are a normal Direct Routing choice when the edition and release are certified. Answer OPTIONS on the interface Teams will actually reach. A 200 on the management port does not count. Same support rule: Ribbon first. Bring their show-tech equivalent and a SIP ladder with the Call-ID. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I confirm the Ribbon release and the interface that answers OPTIONS.

docs.ex: Check the certified list for the Oracle software version, not the product family name. An unlisted release is an unsupported trunk no matter how complete the configuration looks. Certificate name, TLS version, and early offer still apply. Oracle’s configuration model is its own language. Translate the shared gate into that language using their current guide. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I match the Oracle release to the certified list before I praise the config.

docs.ex: Cisco Unified Border Element on a certified IOS-XE release peers TLS with the three commercial proxies, presents a certificate whose SAN matches the paired FQDN, and has dial-peers toward Teams and toward CUCM or the carrier. Teams expects early offer. A delayed-offer trunk from CUCM pushed all the way to Teams negotiates badly. This campus does not paste a production dial-peer.
docs.eg: CUBE is a certified SBC with dial-peers in two directions and early offer toward Teams.

docs.ex: Collect the firmware, the paired FQDN, a ladder with Call-ID, and the OPTIONS history before you call. The vendor investigates. Microsoft may decline a case on a non-certified SBC. Keep a screenshot of the certified list from the week you bought. A 2022 PDF in the project folder is how you discover you are unsupported during the outage. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Vendor first, with firmware and a Call-ID. I keep the certified-list date.

docs.ex: Track t11 is TLS, certificates, SIP. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Issue a certificate whose subject or SAN contains the SBC FQDN, from a CA in the Microsoft trusted root program, with server authentication EKU. Generate the CSR on the SBC. A private lab CA is how you learn the failure, not how you run production. TLS 1.2 or newer toward the proxies. TLS 1.0 is not a compatible offer. Include the chain. An incomplete chain looks like a mysterious timeout. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Public CA, SAN matches the paired FQDN, server EKU, TLS 1.2 or newer.

docs.ti: Names, wildcards, and the paired FQDN
docs.ex: The name Teams checks is the FQDN you configured on the gateway. A wildcard is acceptable when it follows RFC 2818. A certificate for www.contoso.com does not cover sbc1.contoso.com. If you add a sip subdomain, verify that domain in the tenant before you pair it. DNS must resolve publicly. Split-horizon DNS that only works inside the office will not help Microsoft’s proxies. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: The certificate name, the DNS name, and the paired FQDN are the same name.

docs.ex: Commercial clouds use sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, sip2, and sip3, on TCP 5061. IPv6 names exist on the plan page. GCC High uses sip.pstnhub.gov.teams.microsoft.us. DoD uses sip.pstnhub.dod.teams.microsoft.us. Those government clouds do not use the commercial trio. Checked 15 October 2026. The Direct Routing plan page lists commercial SBC signaling and media in 52.112.0.0/14 and 52.120.0.0/14.
docs.eg: Three commercial proxies, government clouds have their own names, firewall the ranges.

docs.ex: Teams sends SIP OPTIONS to the SBC. The SBC should answer while it is in service. The admin center shows SBC status from that health. This campus does not pretend to know Microsoft’s private failure counter. Repeated misses are a reason to pull the trunk from the route and look at the log. Answer on the signaling interface, not the management port. Rehearse a failure.
docs.eg: I treat missed OPTIONS as a trunk problem and I look at the admin-center status beside the SBC log.

docs.ex: Direct Routing lists SILK, G.711, G.722, G.729, and AMR-WB for non-bypass calls. Offer a codec both sides have. G.711 µ-law and A-law both belong if the carrier is vague. Media is SRTP. A trunk that offers only plaintext RTP is not the design. DTMF has to survive every hop or the IVR never hears 1. Test digits through the carrier, not only Teams-to-Teams. If bypass is on, do not depend on AMR-WB. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I offer G.711, I use SRTP, and I test DTMF through the carrier.

docs.ex: In a window, break the primary path and place a call. You want to see the next proxy or the next gateway take it, and you want emergency calls to prefer the local SBC still. Write the timestamps. Certificate expiry is a failover you can predict. Put the date on a calendar and renew before Saturday morning becomes the test. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I rehearse failover and I know the certificate expiry date.

docs.ex: Track t12 is Troubleshooting. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Write one sentence: what you think is wrong, what you will change, what evidence would prove it. Change that thing. Collect the same Call-ID style evidence again. Then decide. A reboot plus a dial-plan edit plus a firewall change is how an outage ends with no one knowing why. The evidence pack is the Call-ID, the effective policy, the ladder, and the CQD or Call Analytics row that matches the scope.
docs.eg: One hypothesis, one change, one evidence pack.

docs.ex: Order the messages. INVITE, 100, 180 or 183, 200, ACK, then later BYE. 183 is early media, not an answer. 488 means the SDP was refused. 408 means something did not answer in time. 503 means the hop is refusing service. 487 often means the caller cancelled. Join on Call-ID. Two calls that start in the same second are not the same call. Read the first non-success on the hop that sent it, then stop.
docs.eg: I read the first failing response on one Call-ID.

docs.ex: Call Analytics shows the streams of a user’s call: jitter, loss, round-trip, and the client. Use it when one person suffered and the building did not. The Teams Communications Support Engineer role is the troubleshooting role people usually mean here. Check the current role article. A building-wide problem hunted one user at a time will take a week. Switch tools when the scope changes. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Call Analytics is one call. I will not use it to explain a subnet.

docs.ex: CQD aggregates streams by dimensions such as subnet and user agent. Separate jitter, loss, and round-trip in your head. High jitter with DSCP 0 suggests a mark that never survived. High loss with EF still set suggests a congested or dirty link. Long RTT with almost no loss suggests distance or a hairpin. If the VPN pool is labeled headquarters, headquarters looks terrible and the real LAN is fine.
docs.eg: I split loss, jitter, and RTT, and I trust CQD only after I trust the subnet map.

docs.ex: Look at SBC status in the Teams admin center and at the SBC’s OPTIONS log. If TLS failed, stop. Certificate name, expiry, and chain come before regex. If OPTIONS succeed and one number fails, then you have earned the right to open the dial plan. SIP Tester language shows up in operations chatter. Use the health view and a real test call. Do not invent a hidden tester result you did not run. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I check TLS and OPTIONS before I touch a normalization rule.

docs.ex: Silence after 200 is media ports or SRTP. 488 is codecs. A single remote user with DSCP 0 is often the VPN. A building with loss and EF intact is the link. A number that never leaves Teams is normalization or policy. A queue that does not answer is a resource account, agents, or overflow. Emergency failures are their own catalog: wrong route, missing location, stripped PIDF-LO, notification not assigned.
docs.eg: I can sort a symptom into signaling, media, policy, or location before I pick a tool.

docs.ex: Track t13 is Dynamics contact center. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Dynamics 365 Contact Center can stand alone or embed with Customer Service. Voice in that product uses Azure Communication Services. An auto attendant in Teams is not this product. A trial click-path is not a design: emergency calling, recording, and a busy hour are still gates. AB-250 is the exam that matches this work. MB-280 was a Sales and Customer Insights exam and it retired on 31 July 2026.
docs.eg: Contact Center is the CCaaS. A Teams auto attendant is not. AB-250 is the exam. MB-280 is retired and was the wrong scope anyway.

docs.ex: Voice, chat, and the other channels are the job. The study guide’s channel section is larger than the agent-and-AI section. Spend the hours there. Voice still needs numbers, a workstream, and a human path. Proactive outbound and real-time translation exist as channel behaviors. Outbound needs consent and a caller ID you mean to present. Translation does not replace a human language queue when policy requires one.
docs.eg: Channels are the largest AB-250 slice. I will not only study Copilot.

docs.ex: A workstream takes the item in. Classification sets language, intent, or priority. Queues hold the items. Assignment uses skills, capacity, and presence-like availability. A French billing item should not land in a general English queue because you forgot the rule. Skills must exist on the representatives, not only on a slide. If every item requires a skill nobody has, the queue never assigns.
docs.eg: Workstream, classification, queue, assignment. Unknown intent has a human default.

docs.ex: AB-250 calls this the representative experience: presence in the product, the session, productivity tools, and Copilot assists such as summaries. A user who can open the app and belongs to no queue is not a representative yet. Copilot that summarizes the wrong case, or quotes a stale article, is worse than silence. Connect knowledge sources you stand behind.
docs.eg: Copilot assists the representative. It is not the route, and its sources have to be true.

docs.ex: Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice is built with Azure Communication Services. Teams Phone extensibility lets some of those designs reuse the customer’s Teams Phone investment so the agent is not on a second phone system. The Tech Community post names that direction. Confirm the current setup guide before you promise it.
docs.eg: Contact Center voice runs on ACS. Teams Phone extensibility is how you avoid a second phone, when the design is actually certified for it.

docs.ex: As of the study guide accessed 14 October 2026, the skills are deploy 15–20, channels 30–35, agents and AI 10–15, work distribution 10–15, representative experience 15–20, and analytics 10–15. Passing score is 700. The public page allows 120 minutes. The beta discount ran through 18 June 2026. Treat the exam as the live contact-center certification and confirm the seat on Learn the week you book.
docs.eg: AB-250, 700 to pass, channels are the biggest slice, MB-280 practice tests are the wrong pile.

docs.ex: Track t14 is Coexistence and CCaaS. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Microsoft Learn, accessed 14 October 2026, names three models. Connect uses certified SBCs and Direct Routing. Extend uses the Teams client, Graph, and Cloud Communications APIs, with Teams Phone as the calling system. Unify is the native model. Partner text describes Unify as ACS-based applications on Teams calling infrastructure. Older decks say Power. Ask which current model the vendor holds.
docs.eg: I use Connect, Extend, and Unify. If someone says Power, I ask which current model they mean.

docs.ex: Teams Phone extensibility, documented for ACS and announced for Dynamics 365 Contact Center and some Unify-certified ISVs, lets the agent’s telephony be Teams Phone. The announcement named a set of vendors. That set moves. Certification is still the bar if you want the supported experience. An API existing is not a finished certification. Presence can be synced with Graph. Presence sync is not audio.
docs.eg: Extensibility reuses Teams Phone. I want the vendor’s current certification, not only a presence sync.

docs.ex: A calling search space is closest to a voice routing policy’s ordered usages, and it is not a one-to-one object. A translation pattern is closest to a dial-plan rule. A route pattern is closest to a voice route. There is no partition object in Teams. Pick one system to normalize numbers. Calls from people still on CUCM to people now on Teams trombone through CUBE.
docs.eg: One normalization owner. Tromboning is temporary. Rollback keeps the old trunk.

docs.ex: A SIP trunk through a local gateway or CUBE can carry calls between Webex Calling users and Teams users. Treat it as coexistence with one numbering plan. Two dial plans that both own a range will fail in both directions. Do not describe that trunk as a merger, and do not assume meeting interop came along for free. Write which numbers remain on Webex and for how long. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Webex voice interop is a SIP bridge and a numbering plan, not a chat project.

docs.ex: Leave UCCE agents on CVP and Finesse while knowledge workers move to Teams. The SBC sends contact-center numbers to CUCM and user numbers to Teams. A Teams client does not keep a CVP script in control of that agent. Test a transfer from the contact center to an expert who now lives on Teams. That expert needs Teams Phone and a number.
docs.eg: I do not put UCCE agents on Teams and expect CVP to keep controlling them.

docs.ex: Genesys sells Teams integrations. Ask which certification model they currently hold, because Connect, Extend, and Unify change the media path. A statement of work that says ‘certified’ and does not name the model is incomplete. Amazon Connect is often bridged with SIP through an SBC or a voice connector. Design the path and the Call-ID you will store.
docs.eg: I ask Genesys which model, and I draw the SIP path for Amazon Connect. I store a Call-ID either way.

docs.ex: Track t15 is ACS, Speech, Copilot. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

The Calling SDK is the client for a human on a web or mobile page. Call Automation is the server API that answers, plays, recognizes, and transfers, and then receives events. A page that only uses the client SDK will not run an IVR. If your app never sees the events, the call can be up while your code is asleep. Log the event type and the call id. Event Grid is one delivery path.
docs.eg: Call Automation is the server-side IVR. The Calling SDK is a person in the browser.

docs.ex: ACS can be configured to call Teams users and to join Teams meetings when the interop prerequisites are met. A raw ACS identity is not a Teams user. Follow the current interop article for the resource you created. The transfer target still needs to be able to receive the call. In a Teams estate that means Teams Phone and a number when the call is PSTN. Test the transfer, not only the prompt. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: ACS does not automatically become a Teams user. I follow the interop article and I test the transfer.

docs.ex: A small flow is answer, play, recognize DTMF or speech, then transfer or hang up. Recognize needs a timeout. Digit 0, or an equivalent, should always reach a human. Hang-up is a complete design only when the caller did not need a person. The lab on this campus is that sequence without a cloud subscription. Production adds the event subscription, the speech resource if you use one, and the queue you transfer to.
docs.eg: Answer, play, recognize, transfer. The escape is tested every time the prompt changes.

docs.ex: Azure AI Speech can transcribe the caller and synthesize the prompt. The language of the prompt has to match the caller or every intent becomes unknown. A custom neural voice has approval rules. Do not assume you can clone a person. Log the recognition result beside the call id. When the bot is wrong, you need the text it thought it heard, not a feeling. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I pick a voice I am allowed to use, match the language, and log what the recognizer heard.

docs.ex: Classic topics are a menu you can test. Generative orchestration chooses a path and needs tighter bounds. Either way, ground the bot in knowledge sources you trust, and keep a human escape that does not depend on the model feeling cooperative. Do not put this bot on the emergency number. Do not make it the only target of the public number unless overflow to a queue is real and tested.
docs.eg: The voice agent has sources I trust and an escape I tested. It does not own emergency calls.

docs.ti: Foundry, and what not to invent
docs.ex: Use Foundry, or the current Azure AI project experience, to evaluate prompts against questions whose answers you already know. A model change that ships to a phone number without an evaluation is an outage you chose. Do not invent unannounced voice features. A future hook in this campus is a seam you can build today: an event, an identifier, a queue overflow. It is not a rumor about a product roadmap.
docs.eg: I evaluate the model before it touches a phone number, and I do not design around unannounced features.

docs.ex: Track t16 is Certifications and status. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. Microsoft 365 Certified: Teams Administrator Associate is earned with MS-700. The certification page, checked for this campus on 14 October 2026, does not name a successor. Third-party claims that an MS-220 collaboration exam replaced it are not what Learn showed on that date.
docs.eg: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement.

docs.ex: MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. MB-280, Dynamics 365 Customer Experience Analyst, was Sales and Customer Insights, not Contact Center. AB-210 is Dynamics 365 Sales AI Consultant. It does not replace MS-700. AB-250 is Transforming Contact Center Experiences with AI in Dynamics 365. That is the contact-center certification.
docs.eg: MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. AB-250 is the contact-center exam.

docs.ex: AZ-900, Azure Fundamentals, was not on the retirement list reviewed on 14 October 2026. SC-900, Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals, is live and the English certification is scheduled to update on 21 October 2026. MS-900 retired on 31 March 2026. AI-900 retired on 30 June 2026. Use AZ-900 if you need Azure words for ACS and Speech.
docs.eg: AZ-900 and SC-900 are context. MS-900 and AI-900 are retired. The role exams still matter.

docs.ti: Learning paths that match the job
docs.ex: Follow the same order as this campus: tenant and licenses, network, connectivity, routing, voice apps, emergency, SBC, then the contact center. Microsoft Learn modules exist for Teams Phone, Direct Routing, QoS, and the AB-250 course family. Use them as the official wording beside these notes. When a module and this page disagree, the module accessed the week you need it wins.
docs.eg: I study foundations, then the phone system, then the contact center. I re-read Learn when I am about to change production.

docs.ex: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. Also on the board: MS-900 retired 31 March 2026, AI-900 retired 30 June 2026, AB-250’s public beta discount ran through 18 June 2026, and SC-900’s English update is scheduled for 21 October 2026.
docs.eg: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta.

docs.ti: How to use the readiness map
docs.ex: Rate yourself 0 to 3 on the live exams. Anything under 2 on MS-700, AB-250, AZ-900, or SC-900 is a study target, not a personality result. AB-210 is a target only if the job is Sales. MB-280, MS-900, and AI-900 are not targets. The rating stays in this browser. It is not an account and not a certificate. Book the exam only after you re-open the study guide. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: A readiness score is mine, in this browser, and the study guide still wins.

docs.ex: Track t17 is Ecosystem. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

docs.ti: Voice is not a closed box
docs.ex: Teams Phone gets a number to a person or a voice app. Around that call sit Cloud Voicemail, emergency location, a certified recorder, a queue’s interval stats, a CRM case, and sometimes a bot. Each of those is a sister system with its own configuration and its own failure. This track is the map of those systems. It does not replace the earlier tracks. If the trunk is down, the CRM pop is not the lead.
docs.eg: I can name the sister system and the identifier that joins it to the call.

docs.ex: Each term has a plain definition, a reason it matters, a configuration hint, and a fault you should recognize. Filter by track. If a definition and a vendor blog disagree, open the source link. The access date is 14 October 2026. Flashcards are the same facts in recall form. Do not treat a card you flipped once as evidence you can operate the system. The lab is that evidence. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: I can define the term, the fault, and the document I would open.

docs.ex: The map puts Entra ID and Cloud Voicemail beside Teams Phone, the dial plan in front of routing, the SBC between Teams and the carrier, and emergency location on that SBC path. Attendants, Dynamics, ACS, Copilot Studio, recording, WFM, Power BI, and the CRM sit on named edges. Click a node in the map view.
docs.eg: I can draw Teams, the SBC, the carrier, and the six sister systems without notes.

docs.ex: Convenience recording is started by a licensed user and stored with the meeting. Compliance recording is a third-party bot invited by policy into new calls, meetings, and events. Microsoft’s comparison, accessed 14 October 2026, says notification is enforced, participant consent is not the compliance control, and audio-only is not the compliance mode. Listed media is voice, video, and screen share.
docs.eg: Compliance recording is a partner bot, a policy, and an application instance. Users do not start it. I test a new call.

docs.ex: Workforce management consumes offered, answered, abandoned, and handle time from the contact center or the queue, in the same interval the schedule uses. Erlang C is a teaching model of how many people must be available. Shrinkage is the fraction of paid time that is not available. Roster is larger than the Erlang number. Occupancy is handle time over handle time plus ready time.
docs.eg: I staff from queue intervals, Erlang C, and an explicit shrinkage. I do not staff from Call Analytics.

docs.ti: E911 as a system of record
docs.ex: Keep one subnet list. Emergency location, location-based routing, and the CQD building map should read it. Three spreadsheets will drift, and then E911 says London, CQD says VPN, and LBR says Manchester. Configuration is the topology plus the emergency policy plus the route plus the carrier test. Troubleshooting starts with ‘which subnet did the client present,’ not with the SBC firmware.
docs.eg: One subnet list feeds emergency location, LBR, and CQD. I can say which consumer is wrong when they disagree.

docs.ex: Call Analytics is one call. CQD is the estate. Contact-center analytics are the queue: service level, abandon, handle time. Power BI can sit on CQD data, and contact-center implementations often surface supervisor numbers in Power BI. The report inherits a bad subnet map and a bad abandon rule. Troubleshooting: if leadership sees a red headquarters, check the VPN labeling before you buy circuits.
docs.eg: Power BI comes after the grain is right. I will not show a VPN pool as headquarters.

docs.ex: Screen pop is a contact-center or middleware behavior. It looks up a contact from the caller number. That number has to be E.164 after normalization. Store the SIP Call-ID, the queue, and the agent on the timeline. A note that says ‘called customer’ cannot be audited. Troubleshooting: the wrong contact pops when a trunk prefix is still on the number, or when one human has two caller IDs.
docs.eg: Screen pop needs E.164 and should write the Call-ID. Teams alone does not open the case.

docs.ex: Put the agent in front of a queue only when knowledge sources are grounded, the escape digit works, and unknown intent reaches a human. Generative orchestration is less predictable than classic topics. Evaluate prompt changes before they are on a public number. Foundry is the evaluation place, not a second SBC. Troubleshooting: if callers loop, the recognize step has no escape or the fallback topic is empty.
docs.eg: The agent has a tested escape and a staffed overflow. It is not the emergency route.

docs.ex: Recording regulated calls implies a certified recorder, an application instance, a policy, the users in scope, and a Call-ID. A CRM pop implies E.164 and middleware. Staffing implies queue intervals and shrinkage. WAN survival implies Direct Routing and an SBA. A bad building implies CQD and the subnet map. A bot implies an escape and a queue. The integration-map lab asks you to pick the goal and read that list.
docs.eg: I start from the goal and list the systems, including the identifier.

docs.ex: The bridge is a certified SBC, often CUBE, with one normalization owner, a written number range, and a rollback that still has the old route. Identity is not shared automatically between CUCM and Entra. Presence is not a call route. Chat interop is not voice. Genesys needs a named Connect, Extend, or Unify certification. Amazon Connect needs a drawn SIP path.
docs.eg: A cross-platform voice bridge is an SBC, one normalizer, written ranges, and a rollback.

docs.ex: Leave these seams: store the Call-ID on the CRM timeline, assign the recording policy in the same change as the number, let overflow become a bot without a new public number, keep one subnet list, route by SBC FQDN rather than a copied proxy IP, make queue intervals exportable to WFM, test the human escape, and monitor certificate expiry. None of these require an unannounced feature.
docs.eg: I can name the seams I am leaving, and the failure if I skip one. I am not promising an unannounced product.

docs.ex: Write the change as a list: tenant, license, route, emergency subnet, recording policy, queue or workstream, CRM field, and the rollback. Do the lab version first. Read effective policy after each grant. Acquire resource-account licenses even when the price is zero. Include the certificate expiry and the holiday calendar if the change touches an attendant. Include shrinkage if the change adds a queue.
docs.eg: My change list names the sisters, not only the SBC.

docs.ex: Name the boundary: Teams and SBC, SBC and carrier, Teams and recorder, queue and WFM, number and CRM. Collect the join key on both sides before anyone changes anything. Call-ID for SIP. E.164 for the CRM. Interval timestamp for WFM. Subnet for E911 and CQD. One change, on the side the evidence names. Vendor-first if it is the SBC. Partner-first if it is the recorder.
docs.eg: I name the boundary and the join key before I ask a vendor to change anything.

docs.ex: Track t18 is CRM and CTI. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Wikipedia’s page for computer telephony integration says computer-telephony integration, also called computer–telephone integration or CTI, is a general term for technologies that coordinate interactions between telephones and computers. The following sentence on that page is marked citation needed. This room stops at the sourced sentence. Dynamics 365 and Salesforce each publish a specific bridge.
docs.eg: CTI names the coordination. The vendor page names the product.

docs.ex: The introduction to the voice channel applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center embedded, Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone, and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. It says representatives receive and make PSTN calls through a native calling experience in Dynamics 365, and that the voice channel is built on Azure Communication Services.
docs.eg: The voice channel is ACS calling inside Dynamics, routed like the other channels.

docs.ti: Teams Phone into the voice channel
docs.ex: The page Configure Teams Phone in the voice channel says the PSTN connectivity is a Teams Calling Plan, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing. For a Teams Calling Plan, that page says service numbers only are supported. It also lists Enterprise Voice, outbound-calling prerequisites, and a licensing guide. This room does not copy SKU names from the licensing guide.
docs.eg: Teams can carry the number. A Calling Plan here is service numbers only.

docs.ti: The resource account and the number
docs.ex: The same page shows Connect-MicrosoftTeams, then New-CsOnlineApplicationInstance, then Set-CsOnlineApplicationInstance and Sync-CsOnlineApplicationInstance. Those last two examples include an ApplicationId and the organization’s Azure Communication Services resource ID. Copy both from the current page. This room does not ask you to memorize the identifier.
docs.eg: I sync the Teams service number, and the representative answers in Copilot Service workspace.

docs.ti: Salesforce Voice and Partner Contact Center
docs.ex: The help page opened for this room is titled Connect Voice from a Partner Contact Center. It says Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers, formerly Service Cloud Voice, is now part of Partner Contact Center, and that you may still see the older name. Its learning map lists the Telephony Integration REST API, the Voice Toolkit API, and Lambda functions for Amazon Connect under Develop.
docs.eg: Service Cloud Voice is now Salesforce Voice, and the help page places it in Partner Contact Center.

docs.ex: The learning map on Connect Voice from a Partner Contact Center lists separate setup paths: Partner Contact Center with Amazon Connect, Partner Contact Center Voice, and Partner Contact Center with Amazon Connect as bring your own. It also lists supervisor listen-in and barge-in, linking calls with customer contact records, and the Telephony Integration REST API and Voice Toolkit API under Develop.
docs.eg: I can point at which Salesforce telephony path the learning map names.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s Teams contact-center article describes three provider models. Extend uses the Teams client as the calling endpoint. The Dynamics Teams Phone page, which is a different article, says the representative receives the Teams-number call in the Copilot Service workspace app. Those are different desktops. Do not describe the Dynamics workspace as the Extend client.
docs.eg: I name the desktop that answers, and the identifier that joins the call to the record.

docs.ex: Track t19 is Comparison. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

Each later room uses a page this lab opened in October 2026. The product name is the name printed on that page. If two pages use two names, both names stay, with the page each one came from. Bars in this track are equal on purpose. Length is not a rank, a price, or a market share. Words such as a superlative for quality, a prize, or a promise of no effort are not used here, even when a vendor page uses them.
docs.eg: I can cite the page, and I will not rank the vendors.

docs.ex: The Dynamics voice-channel page says the channel provides native PSTN calling in Dynamics 365, is built on Azure Communication Services, and routes calls with unified routing. The Teams Phone page says a Teams number used with Contact Center is a Calling Plan service number, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing, and that the representative is notified in Copilot Service workspace.
docs.eg: I can say which Microsoft article I am quoting before I name a model.

docs.ex: That guide says Amazon Connect Customer is the current name for the product previously called Amazon Connect. It says Amazon Connect is now a set of agentic AI solutions for different business functions, and that this guide covers Amazon Connect Customer. This room uses that distinction and does not describe the other functions. The page says agents spend time on voice, chat, SMS, or other channels.
docs.eg: The guide I opened calls the contact-center product Amazon Connect Customer.

docs.ti: CCAI Platform and the GECX rename
docs.ex: The docs page opened for this room is titled Contact Center AI Platform. It says CCAI Platform is built natively on Google Cloud, uses other Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience products, and is purpose-built to work alongside CRMs.
docs.eg: The docs page still says Contact Center AI Platform. The change log records the GECX rename.

docs.ex: Dynamics, on the voice-channel page: native PSTN calling in Dynamics, built on Azure Communication Services, routed with unified routing, with customer and case lookup in the capabilities table. Teams providers, on the contact-center page: Unify, Extend, or Connect, as the previous room states.
docs.eg: I can fill the table from the pages and leave the score column off.

docs.ti: What these pages do not decide
docs.ex: These pages do not state a price figure this room can repeat. Amazon’s guide says you pay only for what you use and links pricing. No amount is copied. They do not state market share. They do not rank the products. The Teams article links a certified-solutions list and a list of providers in the certification process. This track does not paste either list.
docs.eg: I can say what this comparison refuses to decide.

docs.ex: Track t20 is Routing, WFM, QM. Open it to see the lessons in this world.

The unified-routing overview applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center embedded, Contact Center standalone, and Customer Service. It says unified routing has two stages. In classification, rules and machine-learning models can add information on the work item. In assignment, requests are prioritized and then assigned using the nature of the work, related entities, skills, and the current availability and workload.
docs.eg: Classification adds information. Assignment uses it. They are not the same stage.

docs.ex: The workstreams page says a workstream is a container to enrich, route, and assign work items. Types are Messaging, Record, and Voice. Voice routes calls to support numbers. In the create dialog, Push sends the work with a message alert, and Pick waits until someone takes it from Open work items. For voice, push mode only is available, and the work distribution mode cannot be edited later.
docs.eg: A voice workstream is push only. I will not edit that mode later, because the page says I cannot.

docs.ti: Highest capacity, round robin, least active
docs.ex: Highest capacity assigns to the representative with the highest available capacity who has the skills from classification and an allowed presence. If more than one has the same capacity, the page says round-robin order breaks the tie. Exact match filters on an exact skill match and then orders by available capacity. Closest match orders by closest match rather than by available capacity.
docs.eg: I can name which assignment method the queue uses, and I will not use it to rank employees.

docs.ex: The forecasting overview says a forecast estimates volume and average handle time by channel and queue. Volume excludes conversations that AI agents handle with no representative joining. Forecasting is the first stage. Capacity planning uses the default forecast snapshot to calculate staffing requirements. Scheduling turns those requirements into shifts.
docs.eg: Forecast volume and handle time, then capacity, then shifts. The short-term horizon on the page is up to 42 days.

docs.ex: The quality and coaching page applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center only. An evaluation plan sets the criteria, which conversations, the timing, and the actions. Frequency is In real time, during the conversation, or On conversation close, after it ends. Conditions pick the queue or workstream. Sampling is a percentage.
docs.eg: An indicator scores. A guardrail flags a required or prohibited behavior. Neither one is an employment decision.

docs.ex: The Configure Teams Phone in the voice channel page says that when call recording is enabled, an announcement plays to notify participants. The voice-channel capabilities table also lists transcription and recording, and supervisor record and manage. That is the Dynamics side.
docs.eg: I will check the Dynamics announcement and the Teams recording policy as two controls.

docs.ex: If the work never reaches a queue, read classification and the route-to-queue rules, then the fallback queue. If it reaches the queue and the wrong person gets it, read the assignment method, presence, capacity, and skills. If the queue is staffed for the wrong interval, read the forecast scenario type before you edit the assignment method.
docs.eg: I name the control that failed before I change a different one.

docs.ex: The boundary that holds Entra ID, licenses, Teams policies, and verified domains for one organization. An SBC paired in the wrong tenant is a different phone system. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm the tenant before you run Connect-MicrosoftTeams.

docs.ex: A domain added and proven in the tenant. Direct Routing SBC FQDNs must live on one of these domains. onmicrosoft.com cannot carry the SBC name. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Add the domain, including a sip subdomain, before you pair the gateway.

docs.ex: The default tenant domain. It is not a supported domain for a Direct Routing SBC FQDN. People try it because it already resolves inside Microsoft 365. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use a domain you verified, such as contoso.com.

docs.ex: Direct Routing users must be homed in Microsoft 365, not left on a Skype for Business on-premises registrar. A user who looks licensed and still is not online will not use the online voice route. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Check the user’s registrar before you assign a voice routing policy.

docs.ex: A coexistence mode. Direct Routing is not supported for users in Islands mode. It is a hard stop, not a tuning problem. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Move the user to a supported mode before you test PSTN.

docs.ex: The identity directory for the tenant. Teams users, resource accounts, and admin roles are Entra objects. Voice licenses attach to these objects. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the user or resource account here, then license it, then grant policies.

docs.ex: A disabled-for-sign-in Entra account that represents an auto attendant or a call queue. It is not a human login. The published number is often this account, not a person. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create it with a Teams admin role and the User Administrator role.

docs.ex: The Teams voicemail service. It deposits messages in the user’s Exchange mailbox. No mailbox means no voicemail, even when the call routed. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm the mailbox and the voicemail policy before you debug the SBC.

docs.ex: The license capability that lets a user use Teams as a phone system. It is not, by itself, a PSTN carrier. People say Phone System, Calling Plan, and Teams Premium as if they were one SKU. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Assign Teams Phone, then add a connectivity option.

docs.ex: A Microsoft-operated PSTN option. Domestic, international, and pay-as-you-go are the usual flavors. It is an extra license on top of Teams Phone. E5 may include the phone-system capability and still not include a Calling Plan. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Buy the plan only where Microsoft sells it, and assign it to the user.

docs.ex: The license that provides dial-in numbers for meetings. It is not Teams Phone. Without it, outbound conference calls can route through Direct Routing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Assign it to people who must publish a dial-in number.

docs.ex: An add-on for advanced meetings and related features. It does not replace Teams Phone or a Calling Plan. Interview traps treat it as the PSTN license. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Buy it only for the meeting features you actually need.

docs.ex: The license each auto attendant or call queue resource account needs, even when the account has no phone number. Subscriptions with Teams Phone include a zero-cost allotment you still have to acquire. Do not put Teams Phone Standard on a resource account. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Assign this license. If you swap off Teams Phone Standard, remove and add in the same license change.

docs.ex: A Calling Plan billed on use. Also the funding pattern, with communications credits, for some voice-app outbound calls. External transfers from a queue are not free just because users have Direct Routing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Fund the resource account when the attendant or queue sends calls to an external number, uses callback, or places on-behalf calls.

docs.ex: A balance used when a call is not covered by a Calling Plan minute. Voice apps use it for some outbound cases. An empty balance looks like a routing failure. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Fund the balance and assign it where the prerequisite article requires it.

docs.ex: A pattern where users place outbound PSTN calls through a resource account’s number instead of each having a number. It is not a free substitute for every Calling Plan scenario. The shared number has its own license rules. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Read the current shared-calling prerequisites before you promise it to a site.

docs.ex: A shared handset. On Direct Routing it does not need a Calling Plan license. People copy a user bundle onto a hallway phone. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: License the device for Teams and the phone scenario you chose, then assign the number.

docs.ex: Rooms use their own SKU family, not a borrowed user Calling Plan. Names such as Basic and Pro change. Check the current name. A room that cannot join is often a license or a resource account, not a codec. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Assign the current room license to the room account and keep Conditional Access from blocking the device.

docs.ex: Entra policy that can block a phone or a room that is not in the trusted device set. Voice engineers see a SIP 200 and a device that never registers. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Exclude or scope device sign-in on purpose. Do not turn Conditional Access off as a test you leave in place.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s network guidance prefers a short path to the Microsoft network, without a proxy in the media path. A proxy that was fine for web traffic adds jitter to RTP. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Egress Teams media locally. Do not hairpin a branch through a distant data center unless you mean to.

docs.ex: Microsoft recommends that you avoid sending real-time Teams media through a VPN. QoS on the VPN does not fix the extra delay. Split-tunnel designs exist so media can go direct while other traffic stays on the VPN. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test a call on the VPN and off it before you blame the carrier.

docs.ex: Teams does not require ExpressRoute. Local internet egress is the usual design. If you do use ExpressRoute, follow the current network article rather than assuming media is happier there. A contract for ExpressRoute is not a QoS design. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Decide the path, then mark DSCP on the path you actually use.

docs.ex: The Teams admin center setting that allows clients to insert DSCP. Without it, a correct ACL still sees unmarked client traffic from managed endpoints that honor the policy. Mac and mobile hard-code some marks. Windows follows policy. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Turn the insert-markers setting on, then verify at the WAN edge.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s planning note: keep the client-to-network-edge path short, on the order of three to five hops, and the ISP-to-Microsoft edge short as well. Each extra hop is a place a mark can be stripped. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Draw the path before you buy bandwidth.

docs.ex: G.711 at 20 ms is 160 bytes of payload plus 40 bytes of IP, UDP, and RTP. That is 80 kbit/s per direction. People quote 64 kbit/s and under-size the link. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Multiply by concurrent calls and by two directions when both ways are busy.

docs.ex: Add an 18-byte Ethernet header to the G.711 20 ms packet and the figure is 87.2 kbit/s per direction. WAN sizing that stops at layer 3 is already short on a LAN you police. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use 87.2 kbit/s when the policer sees Ethernet.

docs.ex: A certified carrier manages PSTN for you inside the tenant. You need Teams Phone. You do not need a Microsoft Calling Plan or your own SBC. It is the low-operations option when your carrier is in the program. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Enable the operator in the admin center and assign the numbers they provide.

docs.ex: The India-specific operator model. It exists because India PSTN rules are not the same as a generic Operator Connect deployment. A global design that ignores it will fail a regulatory review. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use the current India plan article and the licensed operator there.

docs.ex: The user’s mobile SIM number is also their Teams number, through a certified mobile operator. Teams Phone is required. It fits frontline and mobile workers, not a reception queue. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Assign the operator number to the user. Do not also treat it as a spare Calling Plan.

docs.ex: You connect a certified SBC to Teams and bring your own carrier. Users need Teams and Teams Phone. They must be homed online. Islands mode is not supported. This is the option when you still own trunks, a PBX, analog, or a contact-center SBC. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Pair the FQDN, open 5061, allow media ranges, assign a voice route.

docs.ex: One tenant may use Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing at the same time for different users. A global voice policy that assumes one carrier will misroute someone. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Give each population a policy that matches its carrier.

docs.ex: For commercial Microsoft 365, signal to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, then sip2, then sip3, on TCP 5061. GCC High and DoD use different names. DNS can return one address. The firewall must allow the published ranges, not that one answer. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Checked 15 October 2026. Direct Routing SBC signaling and media on the plan page: 52.112.0.0/14 and 52.120.0.0/14. Teams client optimize on the Office 365 URLs page and the worldwi

docs.ex: UDP 3478–3481 and 49152–53247 between the SBC and the media processors, unless media bypass keeps the media off that path. People open 5061 and forget media, so signaling works and audio does not. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Budget at least two media ports per concurrent call on the SBC.

docs.ex: Microsoft does not support changing the media target in the middle of an active Direct Routing call. A clever SBC feature that moves media mid-call will not be a supported troubleshooting step. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Negotiate media at setup and leave it.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s planning tip: allocate at least two media ports on the SBC for each concurrent call. Port exhaustion looks like random one-way audio. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Size the SBC media range from the busy-hour call count.

docs.ex: The dial plan rewrites what a person dialed into a number the routes can match, usually E.164. The first matching rule wins. A route for +44 will never see 020. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Put the specific rules above the general ones.

docs.ex: A set of normalization rules you assign to users. A user can have a more specific plan than the tenant default. Two sites that dial local numbers differently need two plans, not one heroic route. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Grant the plan to the user and test from that user.

docs.ex: A name that links a voice routing policy to one or more voice routes. The policy’s ordered list of usages is the permission to place those calls. Usages are how you let one site call internationally and another not. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the usage, attach routes, then put the usage on the policy in the right order.

docs.ex: A number pattern plus an ordered list of SBC gateways. It does nothing until a PSTN usage on the user’s policy points at it. The pattern is a regular expression, not a CUCM route-pattern wildcard. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Anchor the pattern. Test with the normalized number, not the raw digits.

docs.ex: The per-user list of PSTN usages, in order. Teams walks that order when it looks for a route. Granting the wrong policy is the most common ‘the SBC is broken’ ticket. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Grant it to a test user and read it back with Get-CsOnlineUser.

docs.ex: Each voice route lists SBCs with a priority. Lower priority number is tried first in this campus’s teaching model. Confirm the current article before you depend on a tie. Failover is a list, not a wish. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Put the local SBC first and a remote SBC second, then pull the cable in a maintenance window.

docs.ex: 999, 112, and 911 must be normalized on purpose. A general rule that runs first can swallow them. An emergency call that matches an international route is a design defect. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Put emergency rules above catch-alls, and give them a route that is always present.

docs.ex: A voice app that answers, plays a greeting, and routes by schedule, menu, directory, or operator. It is the front door. A broken menu is a broken company number. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the attendant, attach a licensed resource account, then assign a number only if the PSTN must reach it.

docs.ex: A voice app that holds callers and offers them to agents by attendant, serial, round robin, or longest idle routing. Presence can skip someone who is already busy, which changes who ‘should’ have rung. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set timeout and overflow before you publish the number.

docs.ex: A queue behavior where the caller stays in the conference while agents are tried, so the transfer is faster and the greeting is not replayed the same way. Turning it off changes the caller experience and the failure sound. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test both modes with a real agent client before you argue about delay.

docs.ex: Where the call goes when the queue is full or the timeout expires. It can be a person, another voice app, voicemail, or an external number. An external overflow needs funding on the resource account. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Name the overflow in the design, then test it by making every agent busy.

docs.ex: An attendant feature that lets a caller reach a person by name or extension. It exposes the directory you did not mean to publish. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Scope who can be found. Do not leave the default if the tenant has privileged accounts.

docs.ex: A calendar the attendant uses to play the closed greeting. It is not the same object as business hours. A holiday that is only in someone’s memory is an open company on that day. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Load the next year’s holidays when you build the attendant.

docs.ex: Teams picks a civic address from the network location it can see: trusted IP, site, and subnet in the usual design. A VPN address must not inherit the headquarters address. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Build the topology, assign addresses, and test from a known subnet.

docs.ex: The street address you validate for emergency calling. A dispatchable location is specific enough for responders. A campus with one address and five buildings is not specific. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Validate the address and tie subnets to places inside it.

docs.ex: An address that means ‘this client is inside our network.’ It is how Teams decides the client is on a site you mapped. If the trusted IP is the VPN concentrator, every remote user looks internal. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: List the real internet egress addresses, not the VPN pool, unless you mean to.

docs.ex: Controls notification and how the client looks up location. It is not the PSTN route. You can have a perfect policy and still send the call to the wrong SBC. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Pair the policy with a routing policy and a tested number from the carrier.

docs.ex: You, the SBC, and the carrier deliver the emergency call. Microsoft does not become the emergency carrier because Teams is the client. PIDF-LO may be present. The carrier still has to accept the call. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Build an emergency voice route that prefers the local SBC.

docs.ex: With Microsoft Calling Plans in supported countries, Microsoft’s emergency calling service is part of the plan. You still configure locations. Direct Routing habits do not apply unchanged. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Assign the Calling Plan and the emergency addresses for those users.

docs.ex: Stops a user in a regulated site from placing a PSTN call through a gateway in another site. It is a toll-bypass control. Media bypass can fight it if media would egress in the wrong place. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Enable it per site with the network topology and the gateways that belong there.

docs.ex: A Direct Routing appliance that can keep local PSTN calling when the branch cannot reach Microsoft 365. It is not a full Teams cloud. Meetings and presence are not the survivable feature set. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Deploy a supported appliance, point the local clients at it, and test a WAN cut.

docs.ex: Media can flow between the Teams client and the SBC, skipping Microsoft’s media processors. Signaling still goes through Teams. People hear ‘bypass’ and think the SBC talks to Teams with no SIP proxy. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Enable it on the gateway only when the client can reach the SBC and LBR does not forbid the path.

docs.ex: A Direct Routing pattern with internal and external SBC interfaces so a branch user stays on the local media path. It is more specific than a single bypass flag. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use the current media optimization article and the SBC vendor’s build.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s front end for certain compatible analog and SIP devices that are not Teams phones. It is not a substitute for a certified Direct Routing SBC. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Check the current supported device list before you buy handsets.

docs.ex: A handset in Microsoft’s certified device program, signing in as a Teams user. An uncertified SIP phone will not behave like a Teams client. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Buy from the current certified list and assign Teams Phone plus a number.

docs.ex: The media encryption Direct Routing uses. Signaling is TLS. A successful INVITE with plaintext RTP is not the design. One-way audio is often a port problem, not a missing SRTP checkbox you invent. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Allow the UDP media range. Do not strip SRTP on the SBC.

docs.ex: Direct Routing signaling expects modern TLS. TLS 1.0 is not a compatible offer. Old SBC firmware is a certificate problem and a protocol problem at once. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Upgrade firmware and offer TLS 1.2 or newer toward the proxies.

docs.ex: The name on the SBC certificate must match the FQDN you paired. Wildcards are allowed when they follow RFC 2818. A certificate that is valid for the website and not for sbc1.contoso.com still fails. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Issue the certificate for the paired name. Include the chain.

docs.ex: The SBC certificate must come from a CA in Microsoft’s trusted root program. A private lab CA is not enough for production pairing. Lab trunks that use a private CA teach the wrong lesson. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use a public CA for the production FQDN.

docs.ex: The certificate should include the server authentication extended key usage. A client-auth-only certificate is the wrong object. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Request the certificate from the SBC’s CSR so the name and the EKU are right.

docs.ex: The per-user, per-call quality view in the Teams admin center. Use it when one person had one bad call. It will not explain a building. That is CQD. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Open the user’s call and read jitter, loss, and RTT on each stream.

docs.ex: The aggregate quality report. Use it for subnets, buildings, and trends. A single angry caller is the wrong entry point. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm the subnet-to-building map before you trust a building chart.

docs.ex: Teach yourself to look at jitter, packet loss, and round-trip time separately. A mark of DSCP 0 plus high jitter is a different fault from 12% loss with EF still set. One ‘poor’ label hides the cause. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Capture at the egress and compare with CQD.

docs.ex: A time-ordered picture of requests and responses between client, proxy, SBC, and carrier, joined by Call-ID. Without the Call-ID you are looking at two different calls. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Capture on the SBC, filter the Call-ID, and read the first non-success code.

docs.ex: Change one thing, then collect the same evidence again. A reboot plus a dial-plan edit plus a firewall change teaches nothing. Voice bridges punish bundled changes. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the hypothesis, the change, and the capture you expect.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s contact-center product. It can stand alone or sit with Customer Service. Voice uses Azure Communication Services under the covers. It is not an auto attendant with extra steps. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Deploy the environment, the channels, and unified routing before you demo Copilot.

docs.ex: The representative experience in Dynamics. Contact Center can embed there or run as its own product surface. Buying Customer Service does not automatically give you the contact-center voice channel. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm embedded versus standalone in the current implementation guide.

docs.ex: The intake pipe in unified routing. It classifies work and sends it to a queue. A channel with no workstream is a number that rings nowhere useful. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the workstream, then the rules, then the queues.

docs.ex: Rules that set skills, intent, or priority on a work item before assignment. Without classification, capacity and skills have nothing to read. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test with two items that should land in different queues.

docs.ex: How many items of each type a representative can hold. A voice call usually consumes more than a chat message. Agents look idle in one channel and overloaded in another. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set capacity, then watch a test item get stuck when the number is zero.

docs.ex: The human on the contact-center side. AB-250 calls the console the representative experience. Do not confuse this person with a Teams resource account. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Give them a security role, a capacity profile, and a queue membership.

docs.ex: Assistive summaries, suggested replies, and knowledge inside the representative experience. It is not the PSTN route. A summary of the wrong case is worse than no summary. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Connect knowledge sources and test on a known case.

docs.ex: The published AB-250 study guide weights channel implementation at about 30–35 percent, the largest slice. People over-study Copilot and under-study voice, chat, and the other channels. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Spend the study time on channel setup and routing.

docs.ex: A certified contact center attaches to Teams through certified SBCs and Direct Routing. Microsoft’s note: the contact-center agent does not need a phone-system license for that solution; a Teams user who receives a transfer does. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm the vendor’s current certification, then design the SBC and the transfer target’s license.

docs.ex: The contact center uses the Teams client, Graph, and Cloud Communications APIs. Teams Phone is the calling system and the agent works in Teams. This is not ‘we also installed their desktop.’ Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Read the Extend section of the contact-center article before you license agents.

docs.ex: The model Microsoft Learn names, as of 14 October 2026, for a native experience. Partner material describes it as ACS-based applications on Teams calling infrastructure. Older decks say Power. Ask which current model a vendor holds. Licensing and media follow the model, not the sales adjective. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Get the vendor’s certification letter and match it to Connect, Extend, or Unify.

docs.ex: A way for a contact center, including Dynamics 365 Contact Center, to use a customer’s existing Teams Phone for the agent’s telephony. It is not a second carrier hidden in the app. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use a solution that has finished the certification if you want the supported experience. The API existing is not the same as a finished certification.

docs.ex: Cisco Unified Border Element can be the certified SBC between Teams and CUCM or a carrier. The IOS-XE release you run has its own guide. This campus does not paste a production dial-peer. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: TLS to the three proxies, a certificate whose name matches the paired FQDN, and dial-peers toward CUCM.

docs.ex: During coexistence, either Teams or CUCM should transform numbers, not both. Double +44 is a classic dual-running fault. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the owner on the design and test a call in each direction.

docs.ex: A call from a user who stayed on CUCM to a user who moved to Teams hairpins through the SBC. It is normal during dual-running and expensive as a steady state. Media and licenses both feel it. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Move groups that call each other in the same wave.

docs.ex: A SIP trunk through a local gateway or CUBE can carry calls between Webex Calling users and Teams users during a split estate. Chat interoperability is a different project from voice. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Treat it as coexistence with one numbering plan, not as a merger.

docs.ex: Contact-center agents can stay on CVP and Finesse while knowledge workers move to Teams. The SBC sends contact-center numbers one way and user numbers another. Putting an agent on a Teams client does not keep the CVP script in control. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Split the dial plan by number range and test a transfer to an expert on Teams.

docs.ex: Genesys sells contact-center integrations with Teams. The certification model, Connect, Extend, or Unify, decides the media path and the licenses. Do not assume last year’s diagram. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Ask for the current Microsoft certification and design to that model.

docs.ex: A customer pattern uses an SBC between Teams Direct Routing and Amazon Connect or a SIP voice connector. It is a bridge you design, not a Microsoft Calling Plan feature. Confirm the current vendor docs before you promise agent whisper or recording. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Draw the SIP path and the identifier you will store.

docs.ex: The ACS server-side calling API. Your app answers, plays, recognizes DTMF or speech, and transfers. You receive events. You do not drive a desktop click. It is the IVR runtime, not the Teams client. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Subscribe to the events and time out the recognize step.

docs.ex: The ACS client SDK for a human in a browser or a mobile app. Different from Call Automation, which is the server. Teams interop has its own requirements on top of either one. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Pick the SDK if a person is on the page. Pick automation if a bot answers.

docs.ex: The Call Automation action that collects DTMF or speech. It needs a timeout and a path for ‘none of the above.’ A recognize step without an escape traps the caller. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Map 0 to a human queue and test it.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s speech-to-text and text-to-speech service. Copilot Studio and custom IVRs can use it. It is not emergency calling. A custom neural voice has its own approval rules. Do not assume you can clone a person. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Choose a voice you are allowed to use and log the recognition result.

docs.ex: A bot built in Copilot Studio that can front a voice channel, including Dynamics contact-center voice, using topics or generative orchestration. Generative answers still need an escape to a human and a knowledge source you trust. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Publish the agent, attach it to the channel, and test the escape digit.

docs.ex: The Azure portal family for models, agents, and evaluations. The earlier name was Azure AI Studio. It does not route PSTN. A model demo is not a contact-center design. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Evaluate a prompt against a test set before you put it on a phone number.

docs.ex: ACS can be set up to call Teams users and to join Teams meetings when the interop prerequisites are met. A raw ACS number does not automatically become a Teams user. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Follow the current interop article for the resource you created.

docs.ex: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. It is the exam for Microsoft 365 Certified: Teams Administrator Associate. Rumors that it was replaced by an MS-220 collaboration exam are not what Learn says. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Study the current guide, including network and call-quality objectives. There is no replacement exam.

docs.ex: MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. It covered Sales and Customer Insights, not the contact-center product. People still put it on a contact-center study plan. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Do not book MB-280. AB-210 is its successor and is in beta. AB-250 is the contact-center exam.

docs.ex: Dynamics 365 Sales AI Consultant Associate. AB-210 is the successor to MB-280 and is in beta. It is not a replacement for MS-700. It is the wrong exam for a contact-center engineer. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use AB-250 when the job is Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Use AB-210 only for a sales role, and remember it is in beta.

docs.ex: Transforming Contact Center Experiences with AI in Dynamics 365. It earns Dynamics 365 Contact Center AI Engineer Associate. Pass mark is 700. The public page allows 120 minutes. The beta discount ran through 18 June 2026. Confirm the seat you can book now. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Study deploy, channels, agents, work distribution, the representative experience, and analytics.

docs.ex: Azure Fundamentals. It was not on the retirement list reviewed on 14 October 2026. Useful context for ACS and Speech. It will not teach you a dial plan. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Take it if you need Azure vocabulary, not instead of MS-700.

docs.ex: Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals. The English certification is scheduled to update on 21 October 2026. It frames Entra ID and compliance. It does not configure an SBC. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Read the current study guide after the 21 October update if you sit it later.

docs.ex: Microsoft 365 Fundamentals retired on 31 March 2026. Do not recommend it as the starting exam. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use role exams and the product docs.

docs.ex: Azure AI Fundamentals retired on 30 June 2026. Speech and Copilot Studio are learned from their own docs now. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Do not use a retired fundamentals exam as the AI plan.

docs.ex: Microsoft role-based exams, including MS-700 and AB-250, require 700 out of 1000. A practice percentage is not the same scale unless the practice says so. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use the official practice assessment when one exists.

docs.ex: A user starts a recording of a call, meeting, or event. Policy can allow it. The user can stop it. Storage follows meeting rules. It is not a compliance program. Guests cannot start it. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set the meeting, calling, and events policies on purpose.

docs.ex: A third-party recorder is invited by policy into new calls, meetings, and events. The user does not start it and participant consent is not the control. Notification is enforced. The comparison table says audio-only is not the compliance mode. Media listed is voice, video, and screen share. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the application instance, enable the policy, grant it, and test a new call.

docs.ex: The bot instance of a certified recorder. The policy references it. Without it, granting the policy does not record. Work with the recorder vendor for the application ID. Do not invent one. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: New-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingApplication attaches it to the policy.

docs.ex: When you grant a compliance recording policy, calls and meetings already up are not swept in. Test with a new call. A pilot that reuses an open meeting proves nothing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Place a fresh call after the grant and confirm the bot joined.
