docs.ex: Listening to and scoring recorded interactions. Often the same vendor as compliance recording, sometimes a separate one. QM needs the recording first. A score without audio is a rumor. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Define the form, the sample, and who may listen.

docs.ex: Scheduling and adherence for a queue. It eats interval stats, handle time, and shrinkage. It is not a feature of a Teams user policy. Teams Call Analytics will not staff next Tuesday. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Feed offered, answered, abandoned, and handle time from the queue or the CCaaS.

docs.ex: The fraction of paid time that is not available for contacts: leave, training, meetings, breaks. Erlang C tells you how many people must be on the phone. Shrinkage tells you how many to roster. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Publish the assumption. A 30 percent guess should be labeled as a guess.

docs.ex: Handle time divided by handle time plus available time. High occupancy feels efficient and burns people out. WFM and quality fight here. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Watch it beside service level, not instead of service level.

docs.ex: The fraction of contacts answered inside a target, for example 80 percent in 20 seconds. Erlang C is one teaching model of it. Averages hide the tail. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the target, the interval, and the abandonment rule.

docs.ex: Power BI can sit on top of Call Quality Dashboard data. It does not replace Call Analytics for one call, and it inherits a bad subnet map. A pretty report of the wrong building is still wrong. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Fix the building and subnet dimensions before you publish a dashboard.

docs.ex: The CRM opens the contact that matches the caller. Teams does not do this by itself for an ordinary PSTN call. The contact center or a middleware has to pass an E.164 number or a case id. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Normalize before the lookup. Store the Call-ID on the timeline.

docs.ex: The international form of a number, starting with + and a country code. Routes and CRM lookups should use it after normalization. Raw digits mean different things in different countries. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Normalize first, then route, then look up.

docs.ex: The SIP header that identifies one dialog. It is the join key between an SBC capture, a carrier ticket, and a CRM note. A timestamp is not an identifier. Two calls start in the same second. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the Call-ID into the system you will have open during an incident.

docs.ex: A named place where another system is allowed to attach: a policy, a queue overflow, a subnet list, an event, an identifier. A seam you do not name becomes a rewrite. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Document the seam in the same change as the feature.

docs.ex: A digit or intent that always reaches a person. Voice agents need one. Emergency numbers need a real route, not a bot. A bot that cannot fail open will trap callers. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test the escape on every prompt change.

docs.ex: The date the SBC certificate stops being valid. It is an integration hook because every carrier and every proxy will notice it on the same morning. Calendar it like a license, not like a surprise. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Monitor the date and renew before the TLS handshake fails.

docs.ex: The same subnet definitions should feed emergency location, location-based routing, and the CQD building report. Three spreadsheets drift. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Give one team the edit right and publish the list.

docs.ex: A 15-minute or 30-minute bucket of offered, answered, and abandoned contacts. WFM and Erlang C both assume you know the bucket. Mixing daily totals into a 30-minute formula is a unit error. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Export the same interval the schedule uses.

docs.ex: A caller who hangs up before an agent answers. Whether short abandons count is a business rule. Two reports with different abandon rules cannot be compared. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the rule down and use it in WFM and in the service-level report.

docs.ex: Talk time plus after-call work, unless your definition says otherwise. Erlang traffic is calls times handle time divided by the interval. A handle time that forgets after-call work understaffs the queue. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Measure it from the contact center, not from a stopwatch on one call.

docs.ex: A location object that can be carried in a SIP INVITE for an emergency call so the far end sees where the caller is. It does not replace a carrier who knows how to route emergency calls in that country. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm the SBC passes it and the carrier reads it.

docs.ex: An emergency calling policy can notify people on site when an emergency call is placed. Security who are not notified will meet the responders in the wrong lobby. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test the notification with the carrier’s test process, not with a real emergency call.

docs.ex: Office 365 GCC High uses sip.pstnhub.gov.teams.microsoft.us. Do not copy the commercial three-proxy list into a government tenant. The commercial names will not be the signaling peers. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Read the plan page for the cloud you are actually in.

docs.ex: Office 365 DoD uses sip.pstnhub.dod.teams.microsoft.us. Same failure as using commercial names in the wrong cloud. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use the DoD name from the current plan page.

docs.ex: The plan page also lists sip.ipv6.pstnhub.microsoft.com and the sip2 and sip3 IPv6 names, resolving into 2603:1063:400::/40. An IPv6-only SBC that was given the IPv4 names never peers. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Match the address family you actually route.

docs.ex: Teams Direct Routing presents media in the INVITE. An SBC or CUBE that waits for a delayed offer will negotiate badly. 488 and one-way audio show up when the offer model is wrong. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set the vendor profile for early offer toward Teams.

docs.ex: A certified SBC family. Mediant devices and their management tools are common in Direct Routing designs. The Microsoft certified list is the support boundary, the vendor guide is the config. Naming the brand is not a design. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Follow AudioCodes’ current Teams document for the firmware you run.

docs.ex: Ribbon’s certified session border controllers are a Direct Routing option. Core and software editions differ. The support path is Ribbon first, then Microsoft if the vendor escalates. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use Ribbon’s current Teams guide and a public certificate.

docs.ex: Oracle Communications Session Border Controller can be certified for Direct Routing on specific releases. Check the Microsoft list for the release, not the logo. An unlisted release is an unsupported trunk. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Match the certified software version and the certificate name.

docs.ex: Cisco Unified Border Element on IOS-XE, when the release is certified, is a normal Direct Routing SBC and the usual bridge to CUCM. CUBE is still an SBC. It does not make Teams ‘speak SCCP.’ Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use Cisco’s current CUBE for Teams guide. Trust the signaling ranges. Present the paired name.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s Direct Routing support boundary: you call the SBC vendor, they escalate to Microsoft if they must. Non-certified SBCs can be refused. Opening a Microsoft case with a homemade SBC wastes the outage. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep the certified-list screenshot with the firmware version.

docs.ex: Fax, door phones, and elevators usually stay on an SBC or SIP Gateway, not on a Teams client. A Calling Plan user license does not give you an elevator phone. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Put analog on the SBC design and test the emergency path from that device.

docs.ex: A queue can skip agents whose Teams presence says they are busy or in a meeting. An agent who never sets presence will take every serial call or none, depending on the rest of the design. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Decide the presence rule and test with one agent in a meeting.

docs.ex: Agents can be allowed to leave a queue. If you forbid it, staffing math must include breaks or they will dodge in other ways. WFM adherence and the queue opt-out flag are the same argument. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Pick one policy and tell the supervisors.

docs.ex: A queue feature that calls the customer back. The prerequisite article treats callback as a case that needs funding on the resource account. Callback is an outbound PSTN call, not a setting with no carrier. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Fund pay-as-you-go or credits, then test one callback.

docs.ex: Microsoft Graph APIs used by Extend and by recording and presence integrations. They are not a SIP trunk. A design that says ‘we will use Graph instead of an SBC’ still needs a PSTN path. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use Graph for the app, and Calling Plans, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing for the telephone network.

docs.ex: The recorder joins as an application because the user’s policy names it. If the bot fails to join, you have a policy, an ID, or a media problem, in that order. Do not start with the carrier. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Check Enabled, the application instance, and the grant, then the vendor’s join log.

docs.ex: Compliance recordings are retained by the partner’s system, not by Teams meeting storage. Convenience recordings follow meeting storage. Legal hold on a mailbox does not automatically hold the partner’s audio. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the retention in the partner contract and test a restore.

docs.ex: The QM scorecard. It should cite behaviors you can hear, not vibes. A form that scores ‘professionalism’ without a definition will not survive an argument. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Publish the form before you score people.

docs.ex: Often a QM vendor feature on the agent desktop. Teams compliance recording’s documented media list is voice, video, and screen share inside the Teams session, which is not the same as a silent desktop recorder. Do not claim Teams records the CRM screen unless the product you bought does. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: If you need the desktop, buy and disclose that recorder.

docs.ex: The table that says which subnet is which building in CQD. It is only as good as the subnets you typed. A wrong building makes a dashboard accuse the wrong LAN. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Reconcile it with the emergency subnet list.

docs.ex: CQD is an admin report, not a personal call history. The people who can open it are the roles you grant, not every user. A manager with no role will ask for a screenshot instead of access. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Grant the smallest role that can see the report.

docs.ex: Time the agent spends in the CRM after the caller hangs up. Include it in handle time if your WFM definition says so. Leaving it out makes Erlang C look generous. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Define it and measure it from the contact-center state, not from memory.

docs.ex: Assignment that prefers a representative who has the skill the classification step wrote on the work item. Skills that exist on a slide and not on the user do nothing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Attach skills to people and to the classification rules, then test a miss.

docs.ex: Classification that uses an intent, often from a bot or a model, to pick a queue. An intent of ‘unknown’ needs a default queue. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Map unknown to a human, not to a retry loop.

docs.ex: Contact-center campaigns that place calls outward. They need a number, a consent story, and a capacity plan. They are not a Teams user’s personal redial. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Follow the current channel article for outbound, and fund the numbers.

docs.ex: A channel feature that can translate a conversation. It is not a substitute for a language queue when the policy says a human must speak the language. Translation errors in a regulated script are your errors. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Decide where translation is allowed and where a skilled human is required.

docs.ex: The documents a Copilot or a generative agent is allowed to quote. If the source is wrong, the answer is wrong with confidence. Ground the agent or do not put it on the phone. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Limit the sources and test questions whose answers you already know.

docs.ex: The Copilot Studio mode that chooses topics and tools from the conversation, as opposed to a rigid topic tree. It needs tighter safety because the path is not a single menu. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep the human escape outside the model’s mood.

docs.ex: The menu-like Copilot Studio design. Predictable and easier to test. Weaker on paraphrase. Use it when the call must follow a script. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the topics, the entities, and the fallback.

docs.ex: One way ACS delivers call events to your app. If the subscription is wrong, your IVR never sees RecognizeCompleted. The call can be up and your code asleep. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Log the event type and the call id.

docs.ex: Digits in the audio path or as telephone-events. IVRs fail when the SBC strips them. A human can talk and the bot never hears 1. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test digits through every SBC, not only Teams-to-Teams.

docs.ex: Silence suppression changes the average bitrate. Do not size a link only from a G.711 average that assumed comfort noise you did not enable. The peak is still the number that fills the queue. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Size for the codec you offer, per direction, at the packetization you set.

docs.ex: The usual voice packet interval in these bandwidth figures. A 10 ms interval doubles the header tax. Changing ptime on the SBC changes the bandwidth you planned. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Lock ptime in the design.

docs.ex: The client waits a little so late packets can still be played. Too small and you hear gaps. Too large and you talk over each other. CQD jitter and the buffer are related and not the same number. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Fix the network before you hunt a hidden buffer setting.

docs.ex: How long a packet takes to go and come back. Long RTT with low loss means distance or hairpin, not a dirty cable. People add bandwidth and the delay stays. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Look at the path. Bypass or local egress may beat a fatter pipe.

docs.ex: A router or VPN that sets the mark back to 0. The client did its job and the path undid it. Verify at the egress, not only on the PC. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Capture outside the VPN.

docs.ex: People who join meetings in a browser do not use the fixed 50000-range client ports. An ACL that only matches those ports misses them. QoS designs that ignore browsers miss a real population. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Say so in the design if many people join from browsers.

docs.ex: Mac, iOS, and Android use hard-coded audio EF and a hard-coded video and sharing mark. They are not the Windows policy object. A Windows-only QoS rollout looks done and is not. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Still enable QoS in the admin center, and mark at the network for devices that will not cooperate.

docs.ex: The current Teams client process name used when you bind a Windows QoS policy. An old policy aimed at the classic client marks nothing. Policy that matches the wrong executable is a silent miss. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Update the policy object and verify with a capture.

docs.ex: The hour you actually size. Average day divided by eight is not a busy hour. Erlang inputs are busy-interval numbers. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Take the busy interval from the contact center, not from a yearly average.

docs.ex: Both PBX and Teams carry live numbers during a move. Rollback needs the old route left intact. A cut with no rollback is a career event. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Move a range, keep the old path, and write the backout.

docs.ex: Moving a public number from one carrier to another. It has a date and a letter of authority. It is not a PowerShell metaphor. Direct Routing can use numbers the carrier already holds, so a port might be unnecessary. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm who owns the number before you promise a weekend cut.

docs.ex: What outbound calls present. Resource-account outbound and user outbound are different policies. A queue that presents a user’s mobile number breaks trust. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set the calling identity on the voice app on purpose.

docs.ex: The audio a queue plays while a caller waits. Licensing and the file both matter, and silence is a choice you should make on purpose. Callers who hear nothing hang up, and abandon looks like a staffing crisis. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Upload a file you have rights to, and test the timeout.

docs.ex: A respectable overflow target when nobody is left to answer. It depends on Cloud Voicemail and a mailbox for the account that owns it. Overflow to voicemail without a mailbox is a dead end. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test the overflow, then check that the message arrived.

docs.ex: The public number on the first voice app. Everything else can be an internal target. People buy a number per menu option and then cannot afford to change the menu. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: One number, many targets, overflow included.

docs.ex: Compliance recording and many Teams policies can be assigned to a group. A user in the wrong group is recorded, or not, as a consequence. Group sprawl is a voice defect. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use a group you can explain, and read the effective policy.

docs.ex: The policy the user actually has after direct assignment and group assignment are resolved. The one you edited may not be it. Get-CsOnlineUser beats the portal memory. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Read the effective value before and after the change.

docs.ex: A tenant that is not production. Pair a lab SBC there. Do not discover certificate behavior on the company trunk. Production is where rollback costs money. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep lab domains and lab certificates obvious.

docs.ex: Cmdlet parameters move between MicrosoftTeams module versions. Read help in the version you are about to run. A blog’s parameter list is not a contract. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Get-Help cmdlet -Parameter * in the lab.

docs.ex: Use the telephony or communications role that can do the task. Global Administrator is not a voice habit. A shared global account makes every later audit useless. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Named admin accounts, voice roles, and Conditional Access for admins.

docs.ex: A number assigned to a resource account or conferencing, as opposed to a user’s personal number. The inventory and the license follow the connectivity option. A user number on a queue is how you lose the queue when the human leaves. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Take service numbers from the carrier or Calling Plan inventory you actually have.

docs.ex: What Teams does with a number you own that is not assigned. Routing it to an attendant is a product choice you should make. Silence on a published-but-unassigned number looks like an outage. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Point unknown numbers at an attendant or a message.

docs.ex: This campus treats repeated missed OPTIONS as a reason to pull a trunk. It does not publish Microsoft’s internal counter as if it were a documented integer. A lab timer is not a contractual timer. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Watch the admin-center SBC status and the SBC’s own OPTIONS log together.

docs.ex: Pull the primary proxy or the primary SBC in a window and prove the next one takes calls. A second gateway that has never received a call is a drawing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Rehearse, then put the result in the runbook.

docs.ex: If the SBC and Teams offer no codec in common, the call fails, often with 488. Adding AMR-WB on a bypass trunk does not fix a G.711 refusal. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Offer G.711 at minimum unless you have a measured reason not to.

docs.ex: A-law and μ-law are both G.711. A trunk that offers the wrong one still often interoperates, and sometimes does not. Offer both if the carrier is vague. This is a one-line SBC change, after you have a capture. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Capture SDP and compare.

docs.ex: The words the queue plays about position or wait. A lie (‘your call is important’) is still a design choice you can decline. Bad messages increase abandon. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Say something true: whether you record, and whether you call back.

docs.ex: Both convenience and compliance recording require participant notification. Compliance does not ask the participant for consent in the comparison Microsoft publishes. A silent compliance recorder is a legal problem, not a clever config. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Confirm the partner’s announcement and test it.

docs.ex: Know whether your recorder and your policy include emergency calls, and follow the rule you were given. Do not route emergency calls into a bot so they can be ‘handled.’ Emergency is a route, a location, and a carrier. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep the emergency voice route boring and local.

docs.ex: The case note should carry the Call-ID, the number in E.164, the queue, and the agent. Then a later complaint can be found. A note that says ‘called customer’ cannot be audited. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Make the screen pop write those fields.

docs.ex: A seam left on purpose for a system you might add later, using a product that already exists. It is not a promise that Microsoft will ship a feature. Invented roadmap items fail audits. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Name the hook, the identifier, and the failure if you skip it.

docs.ex: Older conversation says Power for the third contact-center model. The Learn article maintained on 14 October 2026 says Unify, Extend, and Connect. Using the old word without a mapping hides the media path. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Ask the vendor which of the three current models they hold.

docs.ex: The list of SBCs and contact-center solutions changes. A campus page is not the list. Quote the list the week you buy. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Link the design to the current Microsoft page and the firmware.

docs.ex: In the Connect model, Microsoft’s documentation says the contact-center side does not need a phone-system license, and the Teams user who receives a transferred call does need Teams Phone and a number. Experts who ‘just answer in Teams’ still need a telephone. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: License the humans who receive transfers.

docs.ex: A Dynamics or Teams trial proves a click path. It does not prove emergency calling, recording retention, or a busy hour. Pilots skip the boring gates. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Write the gates: 911, recording, overflow, certificate, rollback.

docs.ex: The numbers go back to the old route if the new path fails. If you deleted the old route, you do not have a rollback. Dual-running exists so rollback is a script, not a rebuild. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep the old trunk until the new path has a quiet week.

docs.ex: Call-ID, the policy you read, the ladder, and the CQD or Call Analytics row. One pack per hypothesis. Verbal ‘it failed’ is not a pack. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Store the pack with the change ticket.

docs.ex: A fictional tenant name used in Microsoft samples and in this campus. It is not a customer. Examples use 555 numbers and example domains so nothing here is someone’s directory. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep lab names obviously fake.

docs.ex: Microsoft’s practice UI for what an exam looks like. It is not the product lab. Use it so the tool is not a surprise. Still study the skills. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Open the sandbox once before the appointment.

docs.ex: Role-based certifications expire unless you pass the free renewal on Learn. Retirement is a different event from expiry. A certification you earned and did not renew is not a retirement of the exam. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Calendar the renewal. Re-read what changed.

docs.ex: When this campus and a study guide disagree, the study guide accessed the week you sit the exam wins. Skills move. The 27 October 2026 MS-700 update is an example. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Re-open the guide before you book.

docs.ex: The device that speaks SIP to Teams and SIP or another protocol to the carrier or PBX, and enforces the edge. Without a certified one, Direct Routing is unsupported. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Pair the FQDN, not a nickname.

docs.ex: A firewall feature that rewrites SIP. It breaks Direct Routing more often than it helps. Microsoft’s network guidance does not want helpers in the media path. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Turn SIP ALG off on the path to the proxies.

docs.ex: Teams must be able to reach the SBC. A purely private address with no public path will not pair. NAT without a stable signaling address is a classic failure. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Publish the signaling address you documented.

docs.ex: Proxy addresses change inside the published ranges. A firewall object built from one lookup goes stale. Allow the range, not the A record you saw today. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Re-read the plan page when you edit the firewall.

docs.ex: The plan page says that if you enable mutual TLS, install the Microsoft trusted roots on the SBC. MTLS is optional in many designs and mandatory in the way you configured. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Match the SBC setting to what you intended.

docs.ex: The gateway setting that allows media to skip Microsoft’s processors. It is not implied by a short ping. Leave it off until the path is drawn. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set it on the paired gateway, then test from the real subnet.

docs.ex: The default media path through Microsoft media processors in the region closest to the call. Use it when bypass is unsafe. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Allow the documented UDP ranges.

docs.ex: Media processors exist in multiple regions. Calls prefer a close one. You do not pick a street address for the processor. A hairpin to a distant egress undoes that preference. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Keep egress local.

docs.ex: A user can be licensed and still not be enabled for Enterprise Voice in the way the tenant expects. Read the user before you test. The symptom is a client that never offers a dial pad. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Read the voice attributes and the license together.

docs.ex: A Teams calling policy controls client calling features. It is not the voice routing policy that selects an SBC. Two policies with similar names get granted backwards. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Grant the routing policy and the calling policy on purpose.

docs.ex: Presenting a service number instead of a personal mobile. It is a policy, not a hope. Wrong caller ID breaks return calls and CRM trust. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set it on the user or the resource account you mean.

docs.ex: Teams translations use tokens such as $1 for a capture group. The first matching rule applies the translation and stops. A $1 with no group copies nothing useful. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test the rule with the raw digit string.

docs.ex: A short rule can turn a 4-digit extension into E.164. It must not run before emergency codes. Extensions and short codes share a length problem. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Order the rules and test 112, 999, 911, and an extension.

docs.ex: The attendant’s holiday set replaces business hours for those dates. Next year’s holidays are a December project. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Load them when you build the attendant.

docs.ex: The attendant’s operator is where zero, and many failures, should land. An attendant with no operator drops people who do not match a menu. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Name a person or a queue.

docs.ex: Directory search should list only the people you intend callers to reach. A wide directory publishes privileged accounts. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Scope it.

docs.ex: Serial routing uses the order of the agent list. Round robin does not. The person on top of a serial list takes the punishment. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Pick the method that matches the promise to the team.

docs.ex: How long the caller waits before overflow. Too short and overflow is the product. Too long and they abandon. Test with agents busy. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set it in the queue and call it.

docs.ex: The audio file must be one you have the right to play. A popular song is not a free hold track. Licensing the song is a legal problem, not a Teams setting. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Use a file you own or have licensed.

docs.ex: Where calls go when the attendant is closed. Voicemail, another number, or a message. Closed with no target is a hang-up. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Set it and call after hours, or fake the schedule in a lab.

docs.ex: A named place in the Teams network topology. Subnets attach to it. Emergency addresses and LBR attach to that story. A site with no subnets does nothing. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the site, then the subnets, then the address.

docs.ex: Civic addresses are validated. An unvalidated string is not a location you can trust. A typo in the street number sends responders next door. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Validate, then test from a known subnet.

docs.ex: Wi-Fi clients can roam across subnets that do not match the building you think. The subnet you mapped is the location you will send. A café SSID bridged to HQ is a false floor. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Map only networks you control.

docs.ex: Clients must be able to use the appliance when the cloud path is gone. An appliance with no client configuration is a spare server. Read the current SBA article for how clients select it. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Test with the WAN blocked, from a phone on that site.

docs.ex: The SBA still needs a PSTN path. That is the local SBC and carrier, not a cloud media processor you cannot reach. Survival without a local trunk is a slogan. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Prove a PSTN call with the WAN down.

docs.ex: Rooms need the same DSCP plan as PCs, using the rooms guidance for Windows and Android. A room that sounds worse than a laptop is often unmarked. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Include the room subnet in the ACL.

docs.ex: The phone signs in as its own account. Voicemail and caller ID follow that account. A shared PIN on a former employee’s account is a privacy incident. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Create the device account and the number.

docs.ex: A policy that requires a compliant interactive PC will block a phone or a room. The failure looks like a bad password. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Scope a device path you can explain.

docs.ex: Certification is specific about software. ‘We own AudioCodes’ is not a version. Upgrade without checking the list can move you off support. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Record the version next to the list date.

docs.ex: Both sides must agree the media is SRTP. A gateway forced to RTP/AVP will not complete a normal Direct Routing call. Silence or a failed offer follows. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Capture SDP and read the profile.

docs.ex: The SDP way digits are carried so an IVR can see them even when the audio codec would hide tones. In-band tones through a lossy codec disappear. Checked 2026-10-14.
docs.eg: Offer telephone-event and test a digit.
